entries.title: 1066 and All Wrong
entries.subtitle: England hang six on a leaky France in a bronze match nobody ordered, Pickford waves them all in, and Barney bags three points that buy him precisely nothing
entries.html:
The news that truly mattered this weekend came not from a stadium but from a museum loading bay: the Bayeux Tapestry, seventy-odd metres of eleventh-century wool, is being crated up and shipped to London, with a French minister on hand to assure the world it had survived the crossing in "wonderful state". The thing is, of course, a nine-century-old French boast — Hastings, 1066, the last time England were properly done over by the French, stitched by hand and gloated upon ever since. Somebody in Paris really ought to have paused before lending England a giant embroidered picture of it. Tempting fate is one thing. Framing it and posting it over is quite another.

🇫🇷 France 4-6 🏴óóóóóó England — the bronze nobody ordered, the ten goals everyone got

🇫🇷 France (Sean) against 🏴óóóóóó England (Barney) was the third-place play-off, that dismal consolation staged for a medal neither side crossed an ocean to win — and it duly produced more goals than most of the tournament's serious business combined. For forty-five minutes it was a massacre with Barney's name on it. Declan Rice drilled England ahead inside three minutes, teed up Ezri Konsa's header on 18', and Bukayo Saka struck twice before the interval — the second in first-half stoppage time — for a scarcely believable half-time scoreline of four-nil. England, playing a dead rubber like a cup final; France, apparently still at the buffet.

Then somebody remembered Sean's goalkeeper was in the building. Kylian Mbappé pulled one back on 48', laid on Bradley Barcola for a second on 54', and helped himself again on 66' — a brace and a hand in another, all of it burnishing a Golden Boot he'll collect wearing a bronze medal. Four became four-three, and every ball that beat Seandon Pickford looked less like a save attempted than a wave goodbye. Saka completed his hat-trick from the spot on 87' to steady it, and just when it was safe, the running gag of Joe's entire tournament returned for a curtain call: Ousmane Dembélé — the very footballer spliced into Joe's own gamertag — poked home on 90'+6' to make it five-four, scoring, as ever, for Sean and never once for Joe. Jude Bellingham had the last word two minutes later. Six-four. Pickford: half a dozen conceded and not a single corner he could be blamed for, which for Sean counts as a quiet night.

The reckoning

Three points for Barney, up from 54 to 57, and study that arc — the man who filed for bankruptcy on the Fourth of July, teamless and third, has spent a fortnight clawing back to within three of the summit. There is, alas, one problem with the maths: the summit is closed. Geo was crowned mathematically uncatchable on Wednesday, his 60 points and the £60 already framed on the wall regardless of anything England did tonight. So Barney's bronze-medal heroics move him gloriously nowhere — second before, second after, a whisker adrift of a race already won. No team-league budged either: France sat stuck on 18 in League 1 and, having lost, stays there. Sean banked a flat nothing, watched a stray Dembélé enrich him one final pointless time, and remains fourth on the tiebreak over Joe and a long-becalmed Logan, with Pete bolted to the floor on 31. A ten-goal thriller, and the tables didn't so much as blink.

Looking ahead

And so France and England shuffle off, both eliminated, their tournaments over — which leaves the parish exactly one fixture, and it is the one that has been coming since the semis. The final, Sunday, sets Joe's 🇦🇷 Argentina against Geo's 🇪🇸 Spain: the only two brothers in the whole group marched to the last night of all to settle it between themselves. The headline £60 is already Geo's, so there'll be no fratricide over the big envelope — but do not mistake this for a friendly. Argentina and Spain are dead level on 19 at the top of League 1, and whoever lifts the World Cup lifts the £30 grand-league crown with it. One brother gets the trophy and the cash; the other gets the very long, very quiet drive to Sunday lunch. Tonight was the warm-up act nobody wanted. Tomorrow, the wool comes off.

entries.title: Messi Rows Two Ravens Home, and Barney's Odyssey Sinks in Sight of the Harbour
entries.subtitle: Gordon's volley has England dreaming for half an hour before the old king pulls the strings twice — and the last night now belongs to two brothers and one throne
entries.html:
Every arts desk in the country spent this week on its knees before The Odyssey — "a colossal piece of cinema," the critics swooned — that ancient yarn about a weathered old campaigner who wanders the earth for a decade, everyone assuming he's finished, before he strolls back into his own hall and, without breaking sweat, dismantles the younger men who'd made themselves comfortable in it. The parish need not have queued for a ticket. It got the whole epic live from the semi-final, narrated by a small Argentine in the number ten, and it cost nothing but Barney's soul.

England 1-2 Argentina — the hall is reclaimed

🏴óóóóóó England (Barney) against 🇦🇷 Argentina (Joe) was the tie the whole country had convinced itself was about 1966, and for a glorious half-hour Barney was allowed to believe the ghost story. Anthony Gordon, teed up by Morgan Rogers, lashed a volley home on 55', and England led a World Cup semi-final with the nation squinting into the last of the heatwave and daring to hum the old songs. Thirty minutes of immortality. Thirty minutes in which Barney's season-long thoroughbred, the team he has ridden since the group stage, stood one goal from the final.

And then Odysseus reached for his bow. On 85' Lionel Messi slid Enzo Fernández through to level it, the hall gone suddenly quiet; and on 90'+2', with England reaching for their coats and their excuses, the same old master floated a cross onto the head of Lautaro Martínez, who nodded Barney out of the tournament in stoppage time. Two assists in five minutes for a man everyone had spent a decade calling finished. England did everything right until the precise moment doing everything right stopped being enough. Here ends the story of the Harry Kane — not with a mutiny, but with a header he could only watch drop.

The reckoning

Three well-earned points for Joe, who climbs from 42 to 45 — and study that long, flat form line, because after a fortnight of watching the Dembwélé spliced into his own handle knife him for other men's benefit, Joe has finally strung two wins together and dragged himself off the floor of his own tournament. He remains fifth in the £60 player league, mind; a semi-final win doesn't rewrite a month of famine. But it did something sharper elsewhere: his 🇦🇷 Argentina has vaulted level with Geo's Spain on 19 and, on the tiebreak, seized the League 1 summit outright — the grand £30 crown wrenched off the runaway leader on the very night Joe reached the final.

Barney banked a flat nothing and loses his last live horse, frozen for good on 54. There is a bitter consolation in the ledger — he still holds second in the player league and remains landlord of Leagues 2, 4, 5 and 6, a portfolio of corpses that keep paying rent — but the one team he'd have traded them all for is gone. And spare a thought for the arithmetic at the top: with only Geo's Spain still breathing and Barney unable to add a single point, Geo is now mathematically uncatchable. The £60 is his, scowl and all, whatever happens on Sunday.

Looking ahead

Which leaves the last night of all as a family affair. The final — Sunday 19 July, 20:00 BST — pits Joe's 🇦🇷 Argentina against 🇪🇸 Spain, owned by his own brother Geo: the only two siblings in the parish, marched to the summit of the whole tournament to settle it between themselves. The headline pot is already locked in Geo's name, so there'll be no fratricide over the £60. But make no mistake, there is real blood on this fixture — Argentina and Spain sit level on 19, and whoever wins the final walks off with the League 1 crown as well as the trophy. One brother lifts the World Cup and the £30; the other goes home with the big envelope and a very long, very quiet drive to Sunday lunch.

entries.title: The Scowl Books a Table for the Nineteenth
entries.subtitle: Oyarzabal executes Sean a second time, Spain waltz into the final, and Geo pinches League 1 on the way out the door
entries.html:
Every front page this morning belongs to Barney's England — "the biggest match since 1966," immortality within touching distance, a nation squinting into 30-degree sunshine and daring to dream. Fine. Barney can bask; his 🏴óóóóóó England don't kick a ball until tomorrow. What the bunting brigade rather missed was that the single most important result of the fortnight was quietly filed while they were still ironing their flags.

France 0-2 Spain — the shrug finally meets silence

🇫🇷 France (Sean) against 🇪🇸 Spain (Geo) was the semi the whole draw had been shepherding into existence: the man in fourth, France still lording it over League 1, against the runaway summit-holder who'd already knocked half of Sean's empire out to get here. For a fortnight Sean's France answered every question with a shrug and a goal. Tonight they shrugged, and nothing came.

Note the name on the 22nd-minute penalty: Mikel Oyarzabal. If that has a familiar toll to it, it should — this is the identical marksman whose brace evicted Sean's Austria a fortnight ago. The man has now put Sean in the ground twice in one tournament, a personal vendetta nobody can quite explain. Then, on 58', Dani Olmo threaded Pedro Porro through to settle it, and that was the evening. Two conceded, a spot-kick surrendered, and for once Seandon Pickford had the decency to be beaten rather than embarrass himself — small mercies. France, who'd made a habit of scoring when the meridian told them to, discovered that Geo's men keep even stranger hours.

The reckoning

A cool, characteristically joyless three for Geo, who climbs from 57 to 60 and stretches his lead over an idle Barney (54) back out to six. Study that long form line and it is the same story it has been for a month: a mid-tournament wobble converted into remorseless, unglamorous accumulation, and now a World Cup final on the ledger. He did more than that, mind. His Spain has crept past France's 18 to lead League 1 outright on 19 — a fresh name atop the grand league and a £30 crown prised from Sean's grip in the same night Sean's last team died. That is the whole tournament in one swing: the runaway leader taking the headline pot's rival and his team-league to boot.

Sean banked a flat nothing and now sits teamless, stalled on 46, his patient, fireworks-free climb ending exactly where Geo's throne begins. He holds fourth on the tiebreak over Logan (46), with Joe (42) and a floor-bolted Pete (31) watching the last act from the cheap seats. The League 1 lead Sean carried for a fortnight is gone, and with it France — a side that shrugged its way to a semi and then simply ran out of answers.

Looking ahead

And so Geo's 🇪🇸 Spain march to the final on Sunday 19 July (20:00 BST) — the summit-holder one match from the lot. The opponent, though, the fixture computer keeps firmly behind its back, because it will be the survivor of tomorrow's other semi: Joe's 🇦🇷 Argentina against Barney's 🏴óóóóóó England, the tie the whole country thinks is about 1966 and is, in this parish, about who gets to walk into Geo's path.

Chew on the possibilities. Should Barney's England win the game England thinks is history, the player-league runner-up would meet the leader in a final worth everything — that six-point cushion suddenly a live wire. And should Joe come through instead, the final would set the parish's only two brothers head-to-head on the last night of all, with the biggest prize in the game between them. Geo, for his part, will fancy his chances against either; he has spent this tournament out-lasting men who were sure they had him. One of Joe or Barney books the other half of that final tomorrow. Geo just waits, scowl set, table already reserved.

entries.title: The Man Who Couldn't Lose His Own Grudge Match
entries.subtitle: Bellingham twice sinks Barney's Norway to send Barney's England through, while Joe settles the family score at two in the morning
entries.html:
There is a particular purgatory reserved for the punter who backs both horses in a two-horse race: he holds a winning ticket and a losing one in the same fist, and by the time the photo develops he no longer knows whether to cheer or file a complaint against himself. Barney spent Saturday night in precisely that limbo — a man staging a duel in which the only certainty was that he'd shake his own hand at the end.

Norway 1-2 England (aet) — the house wins, and also loses

🇳🇴 Norway (Barney) against 🏴óóóóóó England (Barney) was the all-Barney reckoning the fixture computer had been threatening since he owned half the draw. Andreas Schjelderup, teed up by Martin Ødegaard, nudged Norway ahead on 36', and for nine minutes Barney was cheerfully beating Barney. Then Jude Bellingham, fed by Anthony Gordon, levelled deep in first-half stoppage time on 45'+2', and settled the whole civil war himself on 93' of extra time — the England man now, per the wires, being fitted for a place among the World Cup's tall stories. It was, by every sober account of the Miami furnace, a lucky and sloppy night's work; one imagines a certain Thomas Tuchel, whose surname doubles as Geo's handle, muttering about mentality on the touchline of a side that isn't even Geo's. No matter. Here comes the story: Barney's England march on, Barney's Norway trudge off, and the wallet is entirely indifferent.

Argentina 3-1 Switzerland (aet) — the family score, settled in the small hours

And so to two in the morning and the fixture nobody in that household could sleep through: 🇦🇷 Argentina (Joe) against 🇨🇭 Switzerland (Geo), the only two brothers in the parish, marched toe-to-toe with a semi-final on the table. Alexis Mac Allister headed Messi's cross home on 10'; Dan Ndoye hauled Geo's grinders level on 67'; and then, on 72', Breel Embolo's red card knocked the last brick out of Switzerland's wall. Down to ten they held on until they couldn't — Julián Álvarez on 112', Lautaro Martínez at 120'+1', and Geo's meticulous 0-0 merchants were finally out-lasted. Note the timing, too: in the real world the Strait of Hormuz slammed shut this very week, and yet the Strait spliced into Joe's own gamertag chose tonight to blow its own door clean off its hinges. The scowl's tournament ends at family hands; Joe's does not.

The reckoning

The night's true winner was Barney, who could not have lost if he'd tried and duly banked three — from 51 to 54, hauling Geo's cushion at the summit from a comfy five down to a nervy three. Study his line: the man who filed for bankruptcy on the Fourth of July, teamless and third, has quietly turned that ruin into a genuine charge on the leader. He also nicked a £30 crown while he was at it — his Norway, knocked out of the tournament tonight, nonetheless stepped over Geo's Mexico to take the lead in League 2, a corpse still collecting rent. Joe took two for the extra-time win, up to 42 and fifth, his Argentina now level with Geo's Spain on 16 in League 1 behind Sean's untouchable France. Geo scraped a single point and keeps the throne on 57, but the lead is shrinking and a team is gone. Logan, Sean (46 apiece) and a floor-bolted Pete (31) watched from the stands.

Looking ahead

The semi-final draws itself into a headline the BBC has already written: Bellingham, with Messi next. 🇦🇷 Argentina (Joe) meet 🏴óóóóóó England (Barney) on Wed 15 July, 20:00 BST — Group J winners against Group L winners, and, far more to the point, the man closing on the summit against the man clinging to fifth, one game from a final. In the other half of the bracket, Geo's Spain still await Sean's France on Tuesday. One of Joe or Barney reaches the showpiece; the other's tournament dies a step from the light — and if Barney's the one left standing, that three-point gap to Geo starts to look less like a lead and more like a countdown.

entries.title: Spain Keep German Hours, and Merino Clocks Off Late Again
entries.subtitle: De Ketelaere's header flatters Sean for four glorious minutes before Belgium are put down at the death — and Geo's reward is a straight semi-final duel with Sean's France
entries.html:
Here is a footnote the parish rarely troubles itself with: Spain keeps the wrong time. Geography files it firmly alongside Britain and Portugal on Greenwich meridian, yet the Spanish clock sits an hour ahead, welded to Central European Time since 1940, when a certain dictator decided it would be politic to keep the same hours as Germany. The upshot is a nation that eats, argues, sleeps and — as it turns out — scores an hour after everyone else assumes the business is done. Fitting, then, that this particular Spain is run by Geo, whose Thomas TwoShell handle carries all the Germanic touchline gravitas the analogy could want. On Friday night his side ran, once again, entirely on German time.

Spain 2-1 Belgium — the winner arrives after the clocks say stop

🇪🇸 Spain (Geo) against 🇧🇪 Belgium (Sean) was the owner-against-owner quarter-final the fixture computer had promised all week: the man on the throne against the man in fourth still chasing him. Fabián Ruiz broke it open on 30', a tidy finish that had Geo's scowl briefly threatening to curdle into a smile. Then, on 41', Charles De Ketelaere rose to meet Timothy Castagne's cross and headed Sean level — the very forward who had put four past Pete's United States a week ago now handing Sean a lifeline right on the interval. For a spell either side of the break it was a genuine wrestle, two group winners refusing to blink.

And then the Spanish clock did its thing. On 88' up popped Mikel Merino to bury the winner — and if that name rings a funereal bell, it should. This is the identical assassin who scored at 90'+1' to execute Pete's Portugal on Monday; a man who has evidently decided the last ten minutes are the only ten worth turning up for. Sean's Belgium, having done everything right for forty-seven minutes, were put in the ground by a striker who keeps far later hours than they do. As for Seandon Pickford between the sticks: two conceded and no more corners to flap at, because there was no more football to play.

The reckoning

A cool, ruthless three for Geo, who climbs from 53 to 56 and — study that long, patient form line — has now converted a mid-tournament wobble into an unbroken run of quiet accumulation at the very top. He was first coming in and he is first leaving, only further away now: his cushion over a becalmed Barney (idle on 51) stretches to five, with Logan and Sean locked together on 46 behind. Sean banked a flat nothing and, worse, loses a horse: Belgium's four-goal swagger from last week counted for exactly nought against a side that scores when the meridian tells it to. He holds fourth on the tiebreak, Belgium bound for the departure lounge. In League 1 nothing toppled — Sean's 🇫🇷 France still lords it on 18 — but Geo's Spain has crept up to 16 and second, close enough now to feel the leader's breath on its neck. No £30 crown changed hands.

Looking ahead

And here the draw serves up its cruel little symmetry. Geo's 🇪🇸 Spain march to a semi-final on Tuesday 14 July (20:00 BST) — and standing in the tunnel opposite will be 🇫🇷 France, owned by none other than Sean. The parish had spent Thursday wondering whether Sean might steer two of his own dugouts into the same last four; instead the man knocked half of his own empire out of the equation tonight, and his surviving side must now avenge Belgium against the very player who eliminated it. The League 1 leader against the League 1 chaser, the fourth-placed man's last team against the runaway summit-holder's first. One adds a final to his ledger; the other's tournament ends where his rival's began. Sean will point to a France that answers every question with a shrug and a goal — but he'll want it settled well before the 88th minute, because Geo's men, on their peculiar Iberian-German clock, only ever seem to wake up when everyone else is reaching for their coat.

entries.title: France Stitch Up Morocco in the Dead of Night
entries.subtitle: The Dembélé in Joe's own handle bags another — for Sean, again — as Sean hauls level with Logan and Logan's last thread is snipped
entries.html:
Somewhere on the M20 last night, under police escort and the sort of hush usually reserved for crown jewels or a witness in fear of his life, a nine-hundred-year-old strip of French embroidery seventy metres long was being smuggled into England — the Bayeux Tapestry, arriving at the British Museum in the dead of night to be gawped at by a nation it once depicted getting comprehensively conquered. There is no polite way to say it: it is a very long, very smug French cartoon about turning up on this island and winning. And it could not have picked a more on-the-nose evening to dock, because a few hours earlier another French masterwork had done precisely the same needlework to a rather less willing subject.

France 2-0 Morocco — the conqueror does it in one seamless panel

🇫🇷 France (Sean) against 🇲🇦 Morocco (Logan) was billed as the meeting of the two men who between them scuttled Barney's entire fleet last weekend, and for an hour it threatened to be a genuine wrestle. Kylian Mbappé saw to the drama early, stepping up on 28' and getting his penalty saved — the second Saturday running, near enough, that a Mbappé spot-kick has been the entire plot until it wasn't. Logan's Morocco, who had strolled so serenely through the earlier rounds, held their needle steady right up to the interval and beyond.

Then the stitching started. On 60' Désiré Doué slipped Mbappé in and the great man made no mistake the second time; six minutes later, on 66', Mbappé turned provider and Ousmane Dembélé buried the second. Savour that one. The Dembélé welded into Joe's own gamertag has spent this tournament knifing him and gilding other men's evenings, and here he was doing it again — a goal that lands on Sean's ledger and nowhere near its namesake's. As for the man in Sean's handle: 2-0, a clean sheet, not a flap at a corner all night, which for Seandon Pickford qualifies as a state occasion.

The reckoning

A tidy, ruthless three for Sean, who climbs from 43 to 46 and hauls himself dead level with Logan — the tiebreak alone keeping Logan a nose ahead in third while Sean sits fourth. Study the form line and it's the same patient, unfussy ascent Sean has been assembling for a fortnight: no fireworks, just a France side that answers every question with a shrug and a goal. Logan, by contrast, banked a flat nothing and watched a rotten night get worse — because the same result that marched his Morocco home also cost him a £30 crown. In League 3, Geo's 🇨🇭 Switzerland has quietly stepped over Morocco's stalled tally to take the leadership Logan held coming in: knocked out of the tournament and out of a team-league in one swing. Up at the summit nothing stirred — Geo idle and untouchable on 53, Barney becalmed on 51 — while Joe (40) and Pete (31) watched from the cheap seats. Sean's France, meanwhile, extends its grip on League 1 to 18, with Joe's Argentina (14) and Geo's Spain (13) trailing in the tapestry's wake.

Looking ahead

France sail on to a semi-final on Tuesday 14 July (20:00 BST), and here the fixture computer keeps its cards pressed to its chest: the opponent is not yet decided, because it will be the survivor of tomorrow's quarter — and tomorrow's quarter, let the parish note, is Geo's 🇪🇸 Spain against Sean's own 🇧🇪 Belgium. Which is to say Sean may yet find himself steering two dugouts into the same semi-final, forced to conquer half of his own empire to reach a final. For Logan's Morocco there is only the exit and the long spectate; the KluivertEye's last exposé filed itself, and now he waits, coat on, to see whether the man he drew level with tonight ends up playing against himself.

entries.title: Two Up, Then the Pharaohs Fold — and a Family Feud Is Booked
entries.subtitle: Enzo's stoppage-time header buries Sean, Switzerland grind Barney out on penalties, and Geo and Joe are marched to a last-eight reunion neither can enjoy
entries.html:
Over at SW19 the bulletins keep circling one word about a 38-year-old who simply refuses to be retired by the calendar: abnormal. "It is not normal," they wrote of Djokovic defying the odds once again — an old master bending a young man's game to his will by sheer refusal to leave. Hold that thought, because Tuesday's last-16 was decided by another ageless number 10 who spent one evening proving both halves of himself at once: the fallible mortal who fluffs a gimme, and the immortal who authors the ending anyway.

Argentina 3-2 Egypt — two goals up, and then the desert swallowed them

🇦🇷 Argentina (Joe) against 🇪🇬 Egypt (Sean) had, for an hour, the look of the great upset. Yasser Ibrahim nodded Egypt in front on 15 from Marawan Attia's cross, Lionel Messi contrived to have a penalty saved on 21 — the great man missing the easy one — and when Mostafa Zico made it 2-0 on 67, Sean's runners-up were an hour from the quarter-finals and the sweetest scalp of the tournament. Then the roof caved in. Cristian Romero headed one back off Messi's delivery on 79; Messi himself volleyed the equaliser on 83, Montiel supplying, penalty sin duly absolved; and Enzo Fernández buried the header at 90'+2' from Lautaro's cross to complete the smash-and-grab. Sean's Egypt — punished from the moment the seeding shoved a mere runner-up into Messi's jaws — led by two and left with nothing, the cruellest arithmetic in the book. Joe's group winners survive by their fingernails.

Switzerland 0-0 Colombia — Geo grinds it out from twelve yards

The nightcap was pure Thomas TwoShell: a taut, scoreless, meticulously joyless 120 minutes between 🇨🇭 Switzerland (Geo) and 🇨🇴 Colombia (Barney), settled in the shootout Geo's scowling touchline seemed to have been rehearsing all along. Not a goal to trouble the scorers, not a moment of hyperpop mischief — just a leftfield edit of a knockout tie, decided on nerve. Switzerland held theirs; Barney's Colombia, group winners of Group K, were marched home having scored precisely nothing across two hours of trying.

The reckoning

The night's one genuine winner was Joe, whose Argentina three lifted him from 37 to 40 — and study the form sheet, because after a fortnight of scuttled ships (Congo DR, Uzbekistan, the lot) the Dembélé-in-his-handle has finally stopped knifing him: three days of quiet gains, and Sean's fourth place now just three points up the road. Geo edged to 53 and holds the summit; Barney, a single shootout-loser's point to 51, stays second and within striking distance. Sean banked a flat zero, his patient climb stalled on 43, an Egypt side that did everything but finish the job now merely a memory. Logan (46, idle) holds third; Pete, out of teams a week ago, remains bolted to the floor on 31. No £30 crown so much as twitched — Sean's 🇫🇷 France still lords League 1, with Joe's Argentina a rung behind on 14.

And here the fixture computer has done something it has resisted all tournament. The quarter-final (Sun 12 Jul, 02:00 BST) pits Joe's 🇦🇷 Argentina against Geo's 🇨🇭 Switzerland — the two brothers of this parish, and the only two, set head-to-head with a last-four place on the table. The leader against the man clawing back off the bottom rungs; the top seed against the grinders who haven't conceded a goal in open play in two knockout ties. One sibling adds a semi-final; the other watches his run end at family hands, in the small hours, with only the referee for company. Geo will fancy another 0-0 and another set of penalties; Joe will point to a side that was two down tonight and simply refused to lose. Keep the kettle on — this one kicks off at two in the morning, and nobody in that household is sleeping through it.

entries.title: Old Gil Checks His Last Two Teams Into the Departure Lounge
entries.subtitle: Merino's 91st-minute dagger and De Ketelaere's brace scrub out Pete's survivors, while Geo tiptoes back onto the throne over a dozing Barney
entries.html:
The record books, that dustiest of holy scriptures, were rewritten at Wembley this week: Harry Styles, it is solemnly attested, has now performed more shows under that famous arch than any human alive — a man who simply would not get off the stage, encore piling upon encore until the ushers gave up and went home. Hold that image of the performer who refuses to accept the house lights, because Monday night's last-16 was decided by two teams who declined, flatly and repeatedly, to leave the building — and by one friend left standing in the empty stalls, coat on, wondering where it all went.

tugal 0-1 Spain \u2014 the winner that arrived after closing time

\ud1 Portugal (Pete) against \\ Spain (Geo) had the look, for ninety long minutes, of a night that would resolve nothing \u2014 goalless, gridlocked, Geo's Tuchelian scowl deepening on the touchline with every squandered half-chance. And then, deep into stoppage time, Mikel Merino did the cruellest thing in football: he scored at 90'+1', turning Ferran Torres's pass into a dagger and a goalless stalemate into an execution. Pete's Portugal \u2014 the very side that had clawed its way through last week's all-Pete civil war \u2014 survived its own reflection only to be put down by the last kick of the evening. Geo's group winners march on without breaking stride.

United States 1-4 Belgium \u2014 two minutes of hope, then the flood

\ud83c\uddfa\ud83c\uddf8 United States (Pete) against \ud83c\udde7\ud83c\uddea Belgium (Sean) was, for a fleeting spell, a contest. Charles De Ketelaere struck on 9, Malik Tillman equalised with a free-kick on 31, and for all of two glorious minutes Pete's hosts were level \u2014 until De Ketelaere headed Trossard's cross home on 33 to end the debate. Hans Vanaken made it three on 57, Romelu Lukaku rubbed it in at 90'+3', and the man welded to Jordan Pickford watched his Belgians concede one and score four, which around here counts as the goalkeeper having a quiet night. Two Pete teams out, one Sean team through, in the same breath.

The reckoning

Spare, then, more than a thought for Pete. He arrived with two horses in the last 16 and left with neither, banking a flat nothing \u2014 rooted to the floor on 31, sixth and alone, and now truly done for the tournament with not a shirt left to cheer. The form sheet tells the sorry tale: after four straight nights of patient climbing a fortnight ago, Old Gil's line has gone flat as a pancake \u2014 five days now welded to 31, and the ushers have the lights on. Up top, the throne changed hands without a ball being kicked in anger by its new occupant: Geo's Spain three lifted him from 49 to 52, and he strode straight back past a stationary Barney (idle on 50) into first place \u2014 the summit reclaimed while the deposed leader dozed. Sean's three make it 43 and a steady fourth. Logan (46, idle) holds third, Joe (37) fifth. No \u00a330 crown moved \u2014 Sean's France still lords League 1 \u2014 but the headline pot has its old name back on it.

Looking ahead

The quarter-final draw has served up a beauty and a betrayal in one: Geo's \ud83c\uddea\ud83c\uddf8 Spain meet Sean's \ud83c\udde7\ud83c\uddea Belgium (Fri 10 Jul, 20:00 BST) \u2014 two group winners, two top seeds, and a straight owner-against-owner duel between the freshly re-crowned leader and the fourth-placed man chasing him. One adds a semi-final to his ledger; the other's road runs home. Sean will fancy his Belgians' four-goal swagger against anyone; Geo will point, Tuchel-like, to a side that grinds out 1-0s at the death and asks no questions. For Pete's \ud83c\uddf5\ud83c\uddf9 Portugal and \ud83c\uddfa\ud83c\uddf8 United States there is only the exit and the long, quiet spectate \u2014 while the man who has run out of teams watches everyone above him keep playing.

entries.title: The Bankrupt Buys Back the Whole Street
entries.subtitle: Two of Barney's teams win, one of Barney's teams must now dump the other out, and Geo's crown goes dark with the Azteca floodlights
entries.html:
Cast the mind back to a certain Whitehall directive, signed a few days ago with the gravity of a man authorising a moon landing: the nation's pubs, it was decreed, could stay open until five in the morning for England versus Mexico. The fixture computer duly manufactured the tie, the licensing gods duly blessed it, and so the parish sat blearily conscious at 2am watching a match that turned out to be worth every minute of lost sleep — and worth, to precisely one man, an absolute fortune. Two nights ago Barney was filing for bankruptcy on the Fourth, both his knockout horses detonating on the launch pad. Tonight the bankrupt strolled back onto the trading floor and bought the entire street.

Mexico 2-3 England — the lock-in earns its keep

🇲🇽 Mexico (Geo) against 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 England (Barney) was billed as the summit-holder against the man chasing him, and for thirty-six minutes it was a taut, wary thing — until Jude Bellingham headed England in front off Bukayo Saka's delivery, then struck again two minutes later with Harry Kane turning provider. Julián Quiñones volleyed one back for Geo's men on 42 to keep the Azteca honest, and when Jarell Quansah was sent off on 54 the whole gamble wobbled: England, a goal to the good and a man to the bad, suddenly had to survive an hour with ten. Kane settled the nerves from the penalty spot on 60; Raúl Jiménez answered from twelve yards on 69 to make it a proper white-knuckle finish; and then England simply dug in and refused to be moved. Geo's group winners are marched out of their own tournament, and the man welded to Harry Kane banked the lot.

Brazil 1-2 Norway — the exposé that came a decade too late

The other half of Barney's evening was, if anything, more improbable. 🇧🇷 Brazil (Logan), top seeds and group winners, spurned the perfect start when Bruno Guimarães had a penalty saved on 14, and the miss hung over the whole night like a bad omen. 🇳🇴 Norway (Barney's second string) waited, and waited, and then let Erling Haaland do what Haaland does — a header from Andreas Schjelderup's cross on 79, and a second from the same supplier on 90 to bury it. Neymar's penalty ten minutes into stoppage time was a receipt for a purchase nobody made: a consolation filed so late the KluivertEye's men had already been shown the door. Logan's tournament-favourite scalp, gone, and not a point in it for a man who sat idle all night and watched a top seed take his ranking down with it.

The reckoning

Study the form sheet and marvel. Barney's climb has been the slow, patient kind — a point here, three there, no fireworks — and tonight it finally crested: six in one sitting hauling him from 44 to 50, and from third all the way to first. The man who three days ago couldn't rub two points together now sits alone atop the £60 player league. Geo, motionless on 49, is deposed into second having watched his Mexico switched off at the Azteca; Logan (46, idle) slips a rung to third with Brazil's corpse still warm. Sean holds fourth on 40, Joe fifth on 37, Pete welded to the floor on 31. No £30 crown changed hands — Sean's 🇫🇷 France still lords League 1, with Barney's England a rung behind on 13 — but the headline pot has a bold new name on it.

And here is the exquisite catch. The quarter-final draw (Sat 11 Jul, 22:00 BST) pairs 🇳🇴 Norway with 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 England — both Barney's. He is guaranteed a semi-finalist and guaranteed, in the same breath, to be the one who eliminates himself, condemned to sit in two dugouts and hope the correct half of his empire prevails. Kane's men or Haaland's — either way the ledger only pays once. For Logan's Brazil and Geo's Mexico the road runs home, and both idle chasers will spend the wait watching the new leader play a grudge match against his own reflection, unable to lose it and unable, entirely, to win it either.

entries.title: Independence Day, and Barney Files for Bankruptcy
entries.subtitle: Ounahi's brace and Mbappé's spot-kick blow up both his teams on the Fourth, and Logan slips quietly past him into second
entries.html:
Across the United States on Saturday the small matter of a 250th birthday was observed in the only grammar America knows: fireworks by the ton, fighter jets ruled straight across the sky, and, per the bulletins, a garnish of extreme weather to remind everyone who is really in charge. A nation lighting rockets, then, and standing back to watch them go bang. Note the theme, because on the very same night Barney lit two of his own and stood back to watch both of them detonate on the launch pad.

Canada 0-3 Morocco — the scenic route to a hammering

🇨🇦 Canada (Barney) against 🇲🇦 Morocco (Logan) stayed politely goalless through a first half that promised a nervy afternoon, and then the second half arrived like the flyover. Azzedine Ounahi, teed up by Achraf Hakimi, broke it open on 50; Ounahi helped himself to a second on 82 from Brahim Díaz's pass; and Soufiane Rahimi, Díaz again supplying, rubbed it in deep into the eighth minute of stoppage time — 90'+8', a goal scored well after Barney had presumably switched the television off. Barney's Group B runners-up are marched home; Logan's Morocco stroll into the last eight, and the KluivertEye's men had the decency to file the exposé in full public view. The three points also did tidy secondary damage: Morocco (11) prised League 3 clean out of the hands of Geo's 🇨🇭 Switzerland, the landlord relieved of a £30 crown while sitting idle at home.

Paraguay 0-1 France — one penalty, one procession

If the first rocket fizzled, the second barely cleared the tube. 🇵🇾 Paraguay (Barney), the thrifty Group D third-placers who'd sneaked this far on fumes, kept 🇫🇷 France (Sean) honest for seventy minutes — until Kylian Mbappé stepped up and buried a spot-kick, and that was the entire story. A 1-0 to Sean's group winners means the goalkeeper welded into his handle kept a clean sheet without so much as a flap at a corner, which around here counts as front-page news. Sean's tournament-leading side purr onward; Barney's Paraguay join his Canada in the departure lounge, two teams out in one evening and not a single point to rub together.

Relish the symmetry, too: the two sides that took a match apiece to Barney tonight — Logan's Morocco and Sean's France — are the very pair now set on each other. Barney's whole surviving fleet was scuttled by the two teams about to meet in the quarters.

The reckoning

A cruel arithmetic. Barney turned up with two horses, ran both, and banked nothing — and worse than nothing, because a stationary Logan did not even have to break sweat to climb over him. Logan's three lifted him from 43 to 46 and from third to second, quietly reclaiming the ground he'd been shedding since his brief spell on the summit a week ago; Barney, motionless on 44, slid the other way into third without kicking a productive ball. Sean's three make it 40 and fourth — a slow, patient climb that hasn't stalled in a fortnight. Geo sits idle and untouchable on 49, still top of the £60 pot despite the pilfered team-league, spending the night — much like his patron saint Tuchel, off praising Mexico's fans in the papers — being lavishly complimented while doing nothing. Joe (37) and Pete (31) watched the fireworks from the fifth and sixth floors respectively.

Looking ahead

The draw has cooked up a beauty. Logan's 🇲🇦 Morocco meet Sean's 🇫🇷 France in the quarter-final (Thu 9 Jul, 21:00 BST) — the two executioners of Barney's evening now turning their knives on each other, and a straight owner-against-owner duel between second-placed Logan and fourth-placed Sean. One of them adds a semi-final to his ledger; the other's run ends against a man he was standing shoulder-to-shoulder with tonight. For Barney's Canada and Paraguay the road runs only home, and he'll spend the wait watching the pair who dumped him out settle which of them gets to keep climbing — while Geo, above them all, need only sit still a little longer.

entries.title: The Scowl Officiates Two Funerals, Keeps the Corner Office
entries.subtitle: Egypt win the shootout Pickford was born for, Messi limps over the line in extra time, and Barney elbows Logan into second
entries.html:
Over in New York this week a pop empress and a tight end exchanged vows before the assembled and the astonished, the whole thing officiated — of all the improbable clergy — by Adam Sandler, a man whose usual register is a funny voice and a rubber golf club. A wedding, then: two houses joined, witnessed, sealed. Note the direction of travel, because Friday night in the last 32 ran the ceremony backwards. Three ties, three owner-against-owner unions hauled to the altar, and every single one ended not in confetti but in a decree absolute — one friend waved through, the other posted straight home. And nobody signed more divorce papers than Geo, who turned up with two teams and left with neither.

Egypt beat Australia on penalties — the keeper's night, at last

🇦🇺 Australia (Geo) versus 🇪🇬 Egypt (Sean), and for once the man welded to Jordan Pickford got the ending his handle keeps promising. Emam Ashour headed Egypt in front on 13, nodding home Karim Hafez's delivery, before Mohamed Hany's calamitous own goal on 55 dragged Geo's Australians level and off to a shootout — and a tie decided from twelve yards is exactly the stage Sean's namesake was built for. Egypt held their nerve, Sean pocketed the survival, and Geo's Group D runners-up were marched out of the building.

Colombia 1-0 Ghana — the second house falls before Geo's had time to mourn the first

Then the other half of Geo's evening collapsed too. 🇨🇴 Colombia (Barney) needed only fourteen minutes: Jhon Arias struck, teed up by Luis Suárez, and that lone goal was enough to see off 🇬🇭 Ghana (Geo) — the Group L third-placed gate-crashers who'd sweated through the best-thirds lottery only to bow out at the first proper hurdle. Two teams, two exits, one long Tuchelian scowl at a touchline that had nothing left to offer him.

Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde (a.e.t.) — Messi drags Joe through the mangle

🇦🇷 Argentina (Joe) against 🇨🇻 Cape Verde Islands (Logan) should have been a formality and very nearly wasn't. Lionel Messi opened on 29 from Lisandro Martínez's pass; Deroy Duarte levelled on 59; Martínez then bundled Argentina back ahead on 92, only for Sidny Lopes Cabral to make it 2-2 on 103 and turn Logan's tier-eight minnows into genuine giant-killers. In the end it took Diney Borges heading into his own net on 111 to settle it — Logan's bravest afternoon undone by one of his own men. Joe's group winners survive; Cape Verde go home with their heads high and nothing else.

The reckoning

A gloriously perverse night at the top: Geo lost both his teams and stayed champion anyway, a single point nudging him to 49 — the leader whose empire is quietly shedding tenants while the throne holds by sheer momentum. The real mover was Barney, whose Colombia three lifted him to 44 and past a stationary Logan (43) into second; Logan battled 111 minutes for one measly point and got demoted for his trouble. Sean and Joe sit locked together on 37, Sean fourth on the tiebreak and Joe — after weeks of scuttled boats — fifth and finally trending upward again. Pete, idle, remains welded to the floor on 31. No team-league changed hands, though Sean's Egypt now lurks a point off Barney's Canada atop Leagues 4 and 5.

Looking ahead

The Round of 16 has served up a duel to make the whole parish wince: Sean's 🇪🇬 Egypt meet Joe's 🇦🇷 Argentina (Tue 7 Jul, 17:00 BST) — the two men dead level on 37 set on a head-on collision, with only one permitted to leave the room. Savour the cruelty of the seeding, too: Egypt earned their place as runners-up and were rewarded with the group-winning, top-seeded Messi machine, about as unkind a prize as a runner-up can draw. Then Barney's 🇨🇴 Colombia collect Geo's 🇨🇭 Switzerland (Tue 7 Jul, 21:00 BST) — second in the money-league walking straight at first, Barney handed the chance to close the gap on the very man he's chasing. For Geo's Australia and Ghana, and Logan's Cape Verde, the road runs only home — and Logan will spend the wait hoping second place doesn't get any further away.

entries.title: The Scowl Retakes the Penthouse
entries.subtitle: Oyarzabal's brace evicts Sean's Austria, Pete referees a duel against himself, and the last light in Joe's window is switched off
entries.html:
A volunteer rummaging through a British archive this week reportedly unearthed a rare copy of the American Declaration of Independence — all self-evident truths and unalienable rights, sat in a damp box a few thousand miles from home. File it under exquisite irony, because Thursday night in the last 32 was a lesson in the precise opposite: not independence declared but independence denied, small nations dragged back under the imperial boot while the big houses collected. And no landlord collected quite like Geo.

Spain 3-0 Austria — the empire strikes down

🇪🇸 Spain, Geo's group winners, needed no vote and brooked no debate. Mikel Oyarzabal, teed up by Marc Cucurella, opened on 36; Pedro Porro headed in Baena's ball on 66; and Oyarzabal, fed by Cucurella again, helped himself to a second on 89 to make it a stroll. 🇦🇹 Austria, Sean's plucky Group J runners-up, were subjugated without ever getting near a rebellion — and the goalkeeper welded into Sean's handle will have fished three from his net and wondered where the reinforcements were. Geo advances purring; Sean's Austrians are marched home in chains.

Switzerland 2-0 Algeria — and the harbour goes quiet

The second Geo procession was over almost before the anthems faded. Breel Embolo struck on ten, Johan Manzambi supplying, and Dan Ndoye doubled it the very instant the second half kicked off on 46 — 🇨🇭 Switzerland home and dry by the break-and-a-minute. On the wrong end were 🇩🇿 Algeria, Joe's third-placed gate-crashers who had squeaked in the back door and now found it slammed. That was the last vessel in the whole StraitOfHorMousaDembele fleet still afloat; with it sunk, an uneasy calm settles over Joe's waters, and — much like the real Strait this week, all seized ships and shark fishermen — there is nothing left moving on it at all.

Portugal 2-1 Croatia — a man argues with himself, and loses either way

Spare a thought for Pete, condemned to referee a private civil war: 🇵🇹 Portugal against 🇭🇷 Croatia, both his, one owner sat in both dugouts. Ivan Perisic put his Croatia ahead on 53, so Pete's left hand led his right for a quarter of an hour — before Cristiano Ronaldo, ageless and utterly shameless, thumped in a penalty on 68, and Gonçalo Ramos rose to Rafael Leão's cross deep in stoppage time on 90'+4' to settle it. Pete loses a team and keeps a team in the same swing and, in the finest hard-luck-Gil tradition, banks his three without the faintest idea whether to cheer.

The reckoning

This was a counter-coup, filed cold. Three nights ago the throne was lifted from beneath Geo's empty deckchair; on Thursday he strode back and lifted it off Logan — six points hauling him from 42 to 48, from second to top of the £60 player league, while an idle Logan, motionless on 42 for a third straight night, was quietly deposed into second. And Geo twisted the knife in the £30 tables too: his Switzerland (10) prised League 3 clean off Logan's Morocco, on the very evening he pinched Logan's crown. Barney (41, idle) holds third, Sean (36, Austria gone) fourth, Joe (35, fleet scuttled) fifth. Pete's three lifts him to 31 — still rooted to the floor, but his line on the form sheet has climbed four nights running, which is more than the men above him can say.

Looking ahead

The Round of 16 has cooked up another owner-against-owner grudge — and a juicy one. Geo's 🇪🇸 Spain draw Pete's 🇵🇹 Portugal (Mon 6 Jul, 20:00 BST): the newly crowned league leader against the man welded to the basement, with Pete's survivor of his own civil war walking straight into the tournament's form empire. Geo's 🇨🇭 Switzerland play on too (Tue 7 Jul, 21:00 BST) against an opponent still to be decided — so savour the not-knowing rather than guess the name. For Sean's 🇦🇹 Austria, Pete's 🇭🇷 Croatia and Joe's 🇩🇿 Algeria, the road runs only home — and for Joe, with every last boat now in dry dock, the next few days are pure spectating while the summit two feet above him gets further away.

entries.title: The Kane Mutiny, and a Lock-In Until Five
entries.subtitle: Sean's Belgians drag Pete to the last kick of extra time, Barney creeps within a point of the summit, and Joe's Congo DR are shown the door on a school night
entries.html:
Somewhere in Whitehall this week a civil servant signed a directive with the solemn air of a man authorising a moon landing: the nation's pubs, it was decreed, may stay open until five in the morning for England versus Mexico. Note the exquisite timing, because the fixture computer has just gone and manufactured precisely that tie for the last 16 — Barney's England against Geo's Mexico — meaning half of this parish now has a licensed, taxpayer-blessed excuse to be conscious at an hour when honest people are asleep. First, though, the small matter of a Wednesday that had to be survived to earn it.

England 2-1 Congo DR

It began, for Barney, like a fire alarm at breakfast: Brian Cipenga, teed up by Chancel Mbemba, lashed 🇨🇩 Congo DR ahead on seven minutes, and for a good hour Joe's third-placed gate-crashers were dreaming of one last raid on a tournament that never expected them. Then the man bolted into Barney's very handle woke up. Harry Kane headed 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 England level on 75, both times fed by Anthony Gordon, and bundled the winner on 86 — here comes the story of the Harry Kane, arriving fashionably late and settling the argument twice in eleven minutes. England march on; Joe's Congo DR, so gloriously irritating a fortnight ago, are shown the door, and the Strait falls quiet.

Belgium 3-2 Senegal

This was the night's proper horror-show and near-fatal cardiac event. 🇸🇳 Senegal, Pete's runners, led through Habib Diarra on 24 and Ismaïla Sarr on 51, and were four minutes from the last 16. Then Sean's 🇧🇪 Belgium — the goalkeeper welded into his handle presumably having stopped flapping for one evening — remembered they were seeded: Romelu Lukaku on 86, Youri Tielemans heading in Trossard's ball on 89, and the whole thing hauled screaming into extra time, where Tielemans buried a penalty in the 125th minute, the very last kick anybody had left in them. Sean survives by his fingernails; Pete's Senegal are dumped out with the finish line in touching distance.

United States 2-0 Bosnia-Herzegovina

Pete, mercifully, had a second horse. Folarin Balogun poked 🇺🇸 the United States ahead on the stroke of half-time — and then, in a burst of pure Old Gil hard luck, got himself sent off on 64, leaving Pete's men to defend with ten. They managed it with room to spare: Malik Tillman curled in a free-kick on 82 to see off 🇧🇦 Bosnia, and Logan's lowly seventh-seeds went home without a whimper. A hero-then-villain in one American shirt, and Pete still profits.

The reckoning

A curious night at the summit, where the two men on top did precisely nothing and stayed there anyway. Logan's Bosnia lost, Geo didn't play, and the pair of them remain deadlocked on 42 — a lead held by sheer inertia. The mover was Barney, whose Kane-fired three lifted him to 41, now a single, agonising point off the throne. Sean's two for the extra-time escape nudged him to 36 and, tellingly, clean past a stationary Joe (35) into fourth — the man who flatlined then surged now sliding quietly the wrong way. Pete's four is his best return in an age; still rooted to sixth on 28, but no longer welded to the floor. No team-league changed hands.

Looking ahead

The last 16 has laid two owner-against-owner traps. First, the lock-in tie itself: Barney's 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 England meet Geo's 🇲🇽 Mexico (Mon 6 Jul, 01:00 BST) — a 1am kick-off the pubs have been cleared to serve until dawn, and a straight duel between the man one point off top and one of the two men sitting on it. Then Sean's 🇧🇪 Belgium collect Pete's 🇺🇸 United States (Tue 7 Jul, 01:00 BST), the beneficiaries of tonight's two great escapes set on a direct collision. For Joe's Congo DR, Pete's Senegal and Logan's Bosnia, the road runs only home — and Logan will spend the next few days hoping his idle 42 proves sturdier than it looks.

entries.title: Joe's Two Ships Founder on the Same Wretched Tide
entries.subtitle: Geo hauls dead level with Logan at the very summit, Sean pinches the grand league, and the Dembélé in Joe's own handle knifes him once more
entries.html:
The BBC's front page carried, amid the meters and the pensions, a small liturgical bulletin from the England camp: Thomas Tuchel announcing that his side will keep faith with Gareth Southgate's penalty plan — a sentence delivered, one imagines, with that patented touchline scowl, jaw set like a man reading a parking fine aloud. Somewhere in this parish it will have raised a wry eyebrow, because the fellow who carries Tuchel's ghost in his gamertag — Geo, the ThomasTwoShell — spent Tuesday night proving he needs no such plan. His 🇲🇽 Mexico settled the whole argument before the half-hour and never let it near a spot-kick. Preparation for penalties is all very well; not requiring them is better.

France 3-0 Sweden — the curse deepens into cruelty

For weeks now the joke has been that Ousmane Dembélé, the footballer welded into Joe's handle, will do anything for anyone so long as it isn't Joe. On Tuesday the fixture computer stopped merely teasing and went for the throat. 🇫🇷 France, Sean's group winners, dismantled 🇸🇪 Sweden, one of Joe's own last-32 runners — and the pass that unlocked it, teed up for Kylian Mbappé on the stroke of half-time, came from Dembélé's boot. Barcola made it two on 53, Mbappé helped himself to a second on 74, and Joe was left watching the man whose surname he wears set up the goal that buried one of his teams. Sean sails on, purring; Joe's Swedes go home in a box that the Dembélé in his name helpfully carried to the door.

Ivory Coast 1-2 Norway — Haaland closes the second hatch

If one shipwreck were not enough, the earlier tie sank the other. Antonio Nusa, fed by Martin Ødegaard, put 🇳🇴 Norway ahead on 39; Amad Diallo, set up by Nicolas Pépé, hauled Joe's 🇨🇮 Ivory Coast level on 74 and briefly threatened a Strait reopened. Then, on 86, Erling Haaland did what Haaland does and drove Barney's Norwegians through. Both of Joe's live boats, then, torpedoed on the same night — one by Sean, one by Barney — and the trade lanes of the StraitOfHorMousaDembele silted up entirely, a fat round zero on the ledger.

Mexico 2-0 Ecuador — a stroll, then a sending-off

Geo's Mexico were rarely troubled: Julián Quiñones struck on 22, Raúl Jiménez on 31, and the only late drama was Piero Hincapié collecting a red card in the fifth minute of stoppage time — a needless flourish for Logan's 🇪🇨 Ecuador, already beaten, already booked for home.

The reckoning

This was a night of quiet tectonics at the top. Geo's three points dragged him from 39 up to 42, dead level with Logan — the leader who sat idle and watched his four-clear cushion of a week ago vanish to nothing; the summit is now a coin balanced on its edge. Sean's France not only advanced but wrenched the grand League 1 off Logan's Brazil, sitting top on twelve, and his three lifted him to 34. Barney banked three of his own to hold third on 38, his empire of live teams still bulging. And poor Joe — two teams out, no points, marooned on 35 while men climb past — endured the sort of evening that makes a hot streak feel like a distant rumour. Pete, on 24, watched from the floor he has made his own.

Looking ahead

The Round of 16 has arranged a positive ambush for Barney. His 🇳🇴 Norway have earned Logan's 🇧🇷 Brazil (Sun 5 Jul, 21:00 BST) — owner against owner, the two men tied at the top of nothing to do with this and everything to do with it — while his 🇵🇾 Paraguay draw Sean's 🇫🇷 France (Sat 4 Jul, 22:00 BST), thrift meeting the freshly-crowned League 1 leaders. Barney thus carries live teams into ties against both his nearest rivals; whatever happens, he cannot lose all of it. Geo's 🇲🇽 Mexico wait until Mon 6 Jul (01:00 BST) for a foe still to be decided — so savour the not-knowing. For Joe's Ivory Coast and Sweden, and Logan's Ecuador, the road runs only one way: home.

entries.title: The Croupier Who Bet the Whole Wheel
entries.subtitle: Logan backs four of the six runners, loses two without flinching, and strolls onto the summit while Geo's throne is lifted clean off an empty deckchair
entries.html:
Picture, if it helps, the most ruthless figure in any casino: not the high-roller, not the card-counter, but the croupier who has quietly placed a chip on every single number before the ball is even released. Rien ne va plus. Red wins, he collects. Black wins, he collects. Zero, the house's own little dagger, lands — he collects again. He cannot win all of it and he cannot lose all of it; he simply rakes whichever way the wheel spins and walks home heavier than he arrived. On Monday night Logan was that croupier, having somehow drawn four of the six teams on the table, and the wheel, obliging as ever, did the rest.

Brazil 2-1 Japan — Logan against Logan, and the house can't lose

The opener was a private fixture in every sense: 🇧🇷 Brazil versus 🇯🇵 Japan, both Logan's, a man sat across the table from himself with chips on both squares. Kaishu Sano's 29th-minute strike briefly threatened to make Logan's left hand beat his right, before Casemiro nodded in Gabriel Magalhães' delivery on 56 and Gabriel Martinelli, fed by Bruno Guimarães, drove the dagger home in the 95th minute — a winner so late the cleaners were eyeing the aisles. Brazil march on; Japan are dispatched; Logan loses a team and gains a team in the same breath and feels precisely nothing.

Germany 1-1 Paraguay (Paraguay win on penalties) — the autobahn finally dies

If the machine merely coughed on its hard shoulder a fortnight ago, on Monday it expired on the forecourt for good. 🇩🇪 Germany, Logan's tier-two juggernaut and a group winner, were dragged to penalties by 🇵🇾 Paraguay — Barney's side, third-placed, an afterthought of a qualifier. Julio Enciso headed Matías Galarza's cross in on 42, Kai Havertz answered from Florian Wirtz's ball on 54, and from the spot the underdog held its nerve. Savour the perversity: Barney's team scraped in by the skin of its teeth and is now in the last 16, while the lordly seed that swept its group is in the departure lounge. Finishing lower has rarely paid so handsomely.

Netherlands 3-4 Morocco (Morocco win on penalties) — the Strait springs another leak

The night's third coin-toss broke Joe's way for eighty-nine minutes and then betrayed him. Cody Gakpo, teed up by Crysencio Summerville, put 🇳🇱 Netherlands ahead on 72, only for Issa Diop to rise to Chemsdine Talbi's delivery in the 91st and head 🇲🇦 Morocco level — a goal that hauled the tie to penalties and duly settled it. Joe's group-winning Dutch are out; Logan's Morocco sail through. The Strait of HorMousaDembele, having reopened so gloriously last week, sprang a leak at the very worst moment.

The reckoning

This was a coronation by stealth. Logan's five points lifted him from 37 to 42, and the man who began this whole circus dead last on the opening night now sits clean atop the £60 player league — having stepped over Geo, marooned and idle on 39, whose throne was lifted from beneath an empty deckchair while the Tuchel in his name scowled at nothing in particular. The team-leagues bled the same colour: Logan's Brazil (10) wrenched the grand League 1 off Sean's France, and his Morocco (8) prised League 3 from Barney's Canada. Barney took a single shootout point to reach 35 and hold third, his Paraguay nicking League 6 off Joe's Congo DR; Joe, on the same 35, slips to fourth. Sean (31) and Pete (24) watched from the cheap seats.

Looking ahead

The Round of 16 has been kind enough to manufacture a feud: Logan's 🇲🇦 Morocco meet Barney's 🇨🇦 Canada (Sat 4 Jul, 18:00 BST), owner against owner, the new league leader against the man one rung below him on the same day Barney's 🇵🇾 Paraguay play on (Sat 4 Jul, 22:00 BST) against an opponent still to be confirmed. Logan's 🇧🇷 Brazil wait until Sunday (5 Jul, 21:00 BST) for a foe yet unnamed — so two men, Logan and Barney, carry two live teams apiece into the last 16, and at least one of those pairs is set on a direct collision. For Joe's Netherlands and Germany and Japan, there is only the long road home.

entries.title: The Tenant Changes the Locks on the Landlord
entries.subtitle: Eustáquio's 92nd-minute volley evicts Geo, and Canada strolls off owning four of the £30 leagues in a single swing
entries.html:
Bad Bunny, the showbiz wires report, spent the weekend lighting up a London stadium with a history-making set — confetti by the tonne, decibels to loosen fillings, a crowd that will dine out on it until the next ice age. Note, then, that the only stadium business in this little parish that paid out actual money on Sunday was the precise opposite: no support act, no encore, two men, one ball, ninety-odd minutes of patient nothing, and a single note struck so absurdly late the stewards already had the cones stacked. There was no light show. There was only Stephen Eustáquio's right boot, and the small matter of a man's tournament ending under it.

The Round of 32 opens — and the rent book finally bites back

This was the tie Wednesday's draw had kept warm, and it duly arrived: 🇿🇦 South Africa 0-1 🇨🇦 Canada, runner-up against runner-up, Geo's property against Barney's — the latest meeting of the man who once owned every door on the street and the tenant who kept paying him rent. For an hour and a half it was a goalless, airless affair, the sort of game that makes a neutral check whether the clock is broken. Then, deep into stoppage time, on 90'+2', Eustáquio swung a boot through a half-cleared ball and volleyed it home, and Geo's South Africa — eliminated on the night they'd dared to dream — were dumped out of their own competition by the very neighbour they'd been collecting rent from all fortnight. Here comes the story of Barney's Canada: three games as a beaten finalist, one knockout, and the locks changed on the landlord at the death. Somewhere on a touchline, the Tuchel in Geo's name was scowling into the middle distance with proper Germanic disgust.

The reckoning

Make no mistake — this was Barney's night, and a richer one than the single goal suggests. Five points hauled him from fourth to third in the £60 player league on 36, stepping clean over Joe (idle, marooned on 34 and shoved down to fourth) — a quiet vindication of a man whose form has crept steadily upward all tournament rather than spiking and crashing. The real loot, though, was in the team-leagues: Canada's nine points didn't just sit joint-top of the grand League 1 alongside Sean's France and Joe's Argentina — they seized the summit of Leagues 2, 3, 4 and 5 in one evening, evicting Geo's Mexico, Geo's Switzerland, Joe's Ivory Coast and Sean's Egypt from four separate £30 perches at a stroke. One volley, four overtakes. And the exquisite twist for the vanquished: Geo's South Africa, beaten and eliminated, were carried by the knockout-round bonus to the top of Leagues 6 and 7 — a frozen, posthumous lead in two underdog tables they can no longer add a point to. Geo took two points for merely turning up to the last 32 and, gallingly for the rest, that was enough to stretch his player-league lead over the idle Logan (37) out to four. Sean (31) and Pete (24, still welded to the floor) sat the night out entirely.

Looking ahead

For Geo's 🇿🇦 South Africa there is no ahead: eliminated, no fixtures remaining, a Group A runners-up berth that ended one volley short of the last 16 — though the consolation cheques in Leagues 6 and 7 may yet soften the bruise. Barney's 🇨🇦 Canada, by contrast, march on into the Round of 16, their next opponent still to be decided — so savour the suspense rather than the name. What the bracket cannot yet tell us is whether thrift's reward will be a kindly draw or a buzzsaw; for now, the only certainty is that the beaten finalist who kept paying the rent has outlasted his landlord, and walks into the next round with four team-leagues bulging in his pockets.

entries.title: Joe Forces the Strait Wide Open on the Last Night of the Groups
entries.subtitle: Argentina go three from three, Congo DR raid the best-thirds till, and Sean's 96th-minute lifeline only drags Austria into Spain's jaws
entries.html:
There is a peculiar comfort in the old machines that refuse to stop ticking — the lighthouse lamp still turning a century after the keeper died, the grandfather clock that outlives three generations of the family who wound it. So it was on the final night of the group stage, a night curated by men who have read their own obituaries and politely declined them. Luka Modrić, somewhere north of forty, floated in the assist for Croatia's winner; Lionel Messi bent a free-kick into the corner with the unhurried boredom of a man signing receipts. The group phase closed not with the young pretenders but with the relics, still humming away in the dark.

Group J — a perfect Argentina, and Sean's stoppage-time miracle that backfired

🇦🇷 Argentina finished flawless, nine from nine, dismantling 🇯🇴 Jordan 3-1 — Lo Celso's free-kick, a Lautaro Martínez penalty, then Messi's curler on 80, Mousa Al-Tamari's consolation a footnote. Joe banks the lot; Barney's Jordan trudge off bottom, pointless. Alongside it raged the night's great pinball machine: 🇩🇿 Algeria 3-3 🇦🇹 Austria. Arnautović, Sabitzer and a Mahrez double had it level and breathless when, in the 96th minute, Saša Kalajdžić rose to head Sean a single, precious point. That header did more than rescue a draw — it flipped Austria from third to runners-up. The catch? Runners-up draw a buzzsaw. Sean's reward for his late heroics is a date with Spain, while Joe's third-placed Algeria escaped with their tournament intact regardless.

Group K — Barney's borough, and the Strait reopens for Joe

🇨🇴 Colombia and 🇵🇹 Portugal cancelled each other out 0-0, enough to send Barney's Colombians top and Pete's Portugal through second — a quiet point apiece. Then came pure Strait of HorMousaDembele: 🇨🇩 Congo DR 3-1 🇺🇿 Uzbekistan, both Joe's, the trade lanes briefly his and his alone. Shomurodov nicked an early lead before Yoane Wissa's penalty and stoppage-time strike, sandwiching Mayele's effort, turned it round. Congo DR sneak through as a best third; Uzbekistan slink off bottom on minus-nine.

Group L — England stroll, Ghana lose and live

🇵🇦 Panama 0-2 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 England gave the story of the Harry Kane its inevitable verse: Bellingham volleyed, then nodded one onto Kane's head on 67. Barney's England top the group; Pete's Panama finish dead last, beaten, goalless, owner of the wooden spoon. Next door, 🇭🇷 Croatia 2-1 🇬🇭 Ghana saw Sučić strike, Derrick Luckassen volley a leveller, and Modrić tee up Vlašić's 83rd-minute header. Pete takes the win; Geo's Ghana lose and somehow still squeak through third.

And the best-thirds guillotine fell hardest on men sitting in hotel lobbies: Congo DR, Ghana and Algeria all climbed above the line tonight, and in doing so shoved Pete's 🇮🇷 Iran, Geo's 🇰🇷 South Korea and Sean's 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 Scotland out of the tournament without any of them kicking another ball.

The reckoning

This was Joe's night — seven points, his joint-best haul, vaulting him from fifth all the way to third on 34. A man who flatlined for a fortnight has now posted seven, seven and seven on three of his last four outings; the StraitOfHorMousaDembele is unmistakably back in the shipping lanes. His Congo DR even wrenched both League 6 and League 7 off Ghana and Bosnia respectively. At the summit Geo sat motionless and stayed top on 39, Logan idle behind on 37. Barney's four hold him fourth; Pete's four keep Old Gil welded to sixth on 24. Spare a thought for Sean: one point for his glorious last-gasp Austrian leveller, and it dropped him from third to fifth all the same.

Looking ahead

The Round of 32 is a hall of mirrors. Pete draws himself — his 🇭🇷 Croatia meet his 🇵🇹 Portugal (Fri 3 Jul), the two-headed coin made flesh, one team buried with the very whistle that saves the other. Geo's fingerprints are everywhere a knife is pointed: his 🇬🇭 Ghana run into Barney's 🇨🇴 Colombia (Sat 4 Jul), his 🇨🇭 Switzerland into Joe's 🇩🇿 Algeria (Fri 3 Jul), and his 🇪🇸 Spain into Sean's freshly-promoted 🇦🇹 Austria (Thu 2 Jul) — the buzzsaw Sean's own miracle booked him. Barney's 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 England get the gentlest welcome going in Joe's third-placed 🇨🇩 Congo DR (Wed 1 Jul), while Joe's perfect 🇦🇷 Argentina collect Logan's draw-loving 🇨🇻 Cape Verde (Fri 3 Jul) — thrift, finally, meeting its reckoning.

entries.title: The Dembélé in Joe's Name Bags a Hat-Trick — for Sean
entries.subtitle: Cape Verde tiptoe into the last 32 without troubling a single goalkeeper, while Sean's eight-point heist hauls him fifth to third
entries.html:
There is a recurring cruelty in this tournament so exquisite it must be the work of a fixture computer with a personal grudge: the footballer welded into Joe's gamertag, Ousmane Dembélé, simply refuses to play for Joe. On Monday he popped up to win a game for Sean. On Friday night he doubled down, trebled down in fact, helping himself to a first-half hat-trick in someone else's silks while the man whose handle bears his surname banked the grand total of nothing. The Strait of HorMousaDembele has, it seems, been permanently rerouted through Sean's harbour.

Group I — France purr, Pete finally cashes a coupon

🇳🇴 Norway 1-4 🇫🇷 France was the demolition. Dembélé struck on 7, 20 and 32 — a Mbappé-fed double then a Tchouaméni gift — and Désiré Doué nodded a fourth in stoppage time, Thelo Aasgaard's reply and a Strand Larsen penalty (saved, 50') mere footnotes. France finish flawless on nine and snatch the summit of the grand £30 League 1 clean off Geo's Mexico. Barney's Norway lost but qualify second regardless — a defeat worth precisely nought to him. Alongside, 🇸🇳 Senegal 5-0 🇮🇶 Iraq was a massacre lit by Rebin Sulaka's 13th-minute red: Pape Gueye plundered a brace, Diarra, Sarr and Ndiaye the rest. Pete's Senegal sneak through as a best third; Sean's Iraq slink off bottom with minus-eleven and twelve shipped — the sort of leakage that would have a certain goalkeeper hurling his cap into row Z.

Group H — Spain by an inch, Cape Verde by stealth

🇺🇾 Uruguay 0-1 🇪🇸 Spain settled on Álex Baena's 42nd-minute strike (Canobbio sent off in the dying seconds for good measure). Geo's Spain win the group; Barney's Uruguay finish third and, agonisingly, land ninth in the best-thirds queue — the very first man on the wrong side of the velvet rope, out without a kick more to give. Next door, 🇨🇻 Cape Verde 0-0 🇸🇦 Saudi Arabia was peak Logan: three matches, three draws, not one goalkeeper genuinely inconvenienced, and somehow second place. A KluivertEye operation if ever there was — qualification smuggled out under cover of stalemate. Sean's Saudis go home.

Group G — Sean's private borough

Here was a sealed estate: every boot on the pitch belonged to either Sean or Pete. 🇳🇿 New Zealand 1-5 🇧🇪 Belgium saw Trossard help himself to a brace and De Bruyne, Lukaku and Saelemaekers pile on; 🇪🇬 Egypt 1-1 🇮🇷 Iran finished level, Saber's early opener cancelled by Rezaeian after Taremi spurned a spot-kick. Sean owns both qualifiers — Belgium first, Egypt second — while poor Pete owns both that perished, his New Zealand bottom and his Iran a third that, per the final reckoning, missed the cut. A landlord collecting rent from his own ruins.

The reckoning

This was, emphatically, Sean's night: eight points — his fattest haul of the whole tournament — vaulting SeandonPickford from fifth all the way to third on thirty, a man who spent a fortnight idling and has suddenly found fifth gear. He also wrenched League 1 (France) and League 5 (Egypt off Barney's Canada) onto his own mantelpiece. At the top, Geo's three from Spain reclaimed the £60 throne — into the night second, out of it first on thirty-nine — nudging Logan (a solitary Cape Verde point) back to second on thirty-seven. Pete's four kept Old Gil welded to sixth, while Barney and Joe, both motionless on twenty-seven, were quietly stepped over by Sean and shuffled down a rung apiece.

Looking ahead

The Round of 32 has Sean's fingerprints everywhere. His 🇫🇷 France draw the gentlest of welcomes — Joe's third-placed 🇸🇪 Sweden (Tue 30 Jun) — while his 🇧🇪 Belgium meet Pete's plucky 🇸🇳 Senegal (Wed 1 Jul), owner against owner, and his 🇪🇬 Egypt run into Geo's 🇦🇺 Australia (Fri 3 Jul). Savour Sean's own catch-22, too: his runners-up 🇦🇹 Austria are rewarded with Geo's rampant 🇪🇸 Spain (Thu 2 Jul), a buzzsaw a place lower might have spared them. Elsewhere Barney's 🇳🇴 Norway take on Joe's 🇨🇮 Ivory Coast (Tue 30 Jun), and Logan's draw-loving 🇨🇻 Cape Verde — who haven't won a thing yet — collect the ultimate punishment for their thrift in Joe's perfect 🇦🇷 Argentina (Fri 3 Jul).

entries.title: KluivertEye Files the Quiet Coup
entries.subtitle: Germany breaks down on the hard shoulder, Logan owns the tow truck, and a man who began the tournament dead last strolls onto the summit
entries.html:
There is a particular cruelty in German engineering: the whole national mythology rests on the promise that the thing will simply work — that the autobahn has no speed limit because nothing on it ever falters, that precision is a birthright rather than a hope. Which makes the sight of a stricken vehicle steaming gently on the hard shoulder, hazard lights blinking like a confession, so very satisfying. On Thursday night Logan's 🇩🇪 Germany broke down in exactly that fashion — and the beautiful part, the part that pays, is that Logan also happened to own the breakdown truck, the garage and the rival car that sailed past honking.

Group E: the machine conks out

🇪🇨 Ecuador 2-1 🇩🇪 Germany was Logan against Logan, and it began precisely to schedule — Leroy Sané, teed up by Wirtz, lashing Germany ahead inside two minutes. Then the bonnet flew open. Nilson Angulo levelled on nine, Gonzalo Plata struck on 77, and the tier-two juggernaut limped off beaten. No matter: Germany top the group anyway on six, Ecuador slip through as a best third, and Logan banks a profit whichever wing mirror he glances into. Next door, 🇨🇼 Curaçao 0-2 🇨🇮 Ivory Coast was Nicolas Pépé's evening — a brace either side of the hour — sending Joe's Ivorians through second and dumping Barney's plucky Curaçao out bottom, nine conceded and a single point to show for the adventure.

Group F: Joe billed himself, again

🇹🇳 Tunisia 1-3 🇳🇱 Netherlands was an entirely in-house affair: an Ellyes Skhiri own goal on three minutes, Brobbey on seven, and a Jan Paul van Hecke header settling it after Mastouri's brief Tunisian flicker. Joe's Netherlands stroll up as winners; Joe's Tunisia finish stone-bottom, pointless, twelve shipped — a man burying his own tenant. Alongside, 🇯🇵 Japan 1-1 🇸🇪 Sweden saw Maeda nod Logan ahead and Anthony Elanga — fed by Gyökeres — peg it back for Joe, the draw nudging both safely through. Joe ends the night owning three of the four Group F doors and feeling all of them at once.

Group D: heroics for nothing

🇹🇷 Turkey 3-2 🇺🇸 United States was the night's grandest act of futility. Trusty struck early for Pete's Americans, Arda Güler and Baris Alper Yilmaz turned it round, Berhalter levelled — and then Kaan Ayhan won it in the eighth minute of stoppage time, a winner so deep it nearly qualified for the next ice age. For all of it, Sean's Turkey finish bottom and eliminated, while Pete's USA top the group regardless. Three points for Sean, a parting trophy with no shelf to sit on. 🇵🇾 Paraguay 0-0 🇦🇺 Australia, meanwhile, was Barney and Geo shaking hands on a goalless point apiece that sent both through — Australia second, Paraguay riding in as a best third.

The reckoning

This was the slow coup made flesh. Logan — last on the opening night, a man who scraped a single point a day through week one — leaves Thursday top of the £60 player league, four points hauling him to 36 and clean over Geo, who managed only Australia's lone point and surrenders the throne on the same 36. Joe was the night's fattest earner, seven points lifting him level with Barney on 27, and his Ivory Coast wrenched the £30 League 4 off Barney's Canada into the bargain. Sean nudges to 22 on Turkey's pointless triumph; Pete, blanked, stays welded to the floor on 16 — though his USA, at least, march on as group winners.

Looking ahead

The bracket has kept its cruellest gag oven-warm: Logan's 🇯🇵 Japan draw his own 🇧🇷 Brazil (Mon 29 Jun), one whistle to send himself through and bury himself in the same breath. Savour the perversity of his other two, too — group-winning 🇩🇪 Germany are handed the gentle 🇵🇾 Paraguay of Barney (Mon 29 Jun), while third-placed 🇪🇨 Ecuador walk straight into Geo's rampant 🇲🇽 Mexico (Wed 1 Jul); finishing higher bought the softer tie. Joe's 🇳🇱 Netherlands meet Logan's 🇲🇦 Morocco (Tue 30 Jun) and his 🇨🇮 Ivory Coast run into Barney's 🇳🇴 Norway (Tue 30 Jun), while his battered best-third 🇸🇪 Sweden draw the short straw of all — Sean's 🇫🇷 France (Tue 30 Jun). Pete's 🇺🇸 USA face Logan's 🇧🇦 Bosnia (Thu 2 Jul), and Geo's 🇦🇺 Australia get Sean's 🇪🇬 Egypt (Fri 3 Jul). Old Gil, for once, has a runner standing and a grudge to nurse.

entries.title: Geo, Inc. Reopens the Company Store
entries.subtitle: The landlord of Groups A and B collects rent off himself and pockets the throne, while Barney sits idle and watches two men climb straight over him
entries.html:
There used to be a particular kind of town — Pullman, Illinois, say, or any grim little colliery village built to a single man's specification — in which one proprietor owned the houses, the shop, the saloon, the chapel and the burial plot, so that every wage he paid out came straight back through the rent book, and a worker could be born, fleeced, married, fleeced again and finally interred without a penny ever leaving the boss's pocket. On Wednesday night, as Groups A and B clattered shut, Geo ran exactly that kind of operation: he owned nearly every door on the street, set one tenant against another, billed himself for the privilege, and walked away the richest man in the parish.

Group B: the landlord settles his own accounts

🇨🇭 Switzerland 2-1 🇨🇦 Canada was Geo's tenants against Barney's, settled the moment the teams re-emerged: Rubén Vargas struck within seconds of the restart, Johan Manzambi added a second on 57, and Promise David's 76th-minute reply for Canada was a polite knock on a door already bolted. Switzerland top the group on seven; Barney's Canada go through second anyway, a beaten finalist still clutching the boarding pass. Next door, 🇧🇦 Bosnia-Herzegovina 3-1 🇶🇦 Qatar was Logan's side dismantling another of Geo's properties — Kerim Alajbegović, a Mahmoud Abunada own goal and Ermin Mahmić's 80th-minute clincher seeing off Hassan Al-Haydos's lone Qatari flicker.
