Bosnia sneak through as a best third; Geo's Qatar finish stone-bottom on a single point. The man owns the group winner and the group's doormat, and feels nothing either way.

Group C: Logan owns the whole top floor

🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 Scotland 0-3 🇧🇷 Brazil was a brisk, brutal eviction: Vinícius Júnior bookended the first half — a seventh-minute opener and a stoppage-time header — before Matheus Cunha rubber-stamped it. Sean's Scotland finish third on three points and, agonisingly, miss the best-thirds cut, dumped out without ever being in the conversation. Alongside, 🇲🇦 Morocco 4-2 🇭🇹 Haiti was wilder than it should have been: a Yassine Bounou own goal handed Pete an early lead, Wilson Isidor briefly levelled at 2-2, and then Hakimi, Saibari, Rahimi and Gessime Yassine put the matter to bed. Logan thus owns both teams atop Group C, Brazil and Morocco arm in arm into the last thirty-two. Spare a thought for Pete, whose Haiti lose all three and bow out pointless — Old Gil's ledger, blotted to the bitter end.

Group A: a man playing both ends

🇨🇿 Czechia 0-3 🇲🇽 Mexico saw Geo's flawless Mexicans — Chávez, Quiñones and a Fidalgo strike deep in stoppage time — finish a perfect nine and bury Logan's Czechia bottom. And 🇿🇦 South Africa 1-0 🇰🇷 South Korea was Geo versus Geo in its purest form: Thapelo Maseko's 63rd-minute goal sending South Africa through as runners-up and consigning his own South Korea to a third place that, like Scotland, fell just short of the cut.

The reckoning

This was Geo's night by a street: nine points lift him from 26 to 35 and back onto the throne he surrendered on Tuesday, vaulting clean over Barney, who kicked nothing of value, banked nothing, and tumbled from first to third for his idleness. Logan matched the nine — 23 to 32 — and the man who scraped a point a day through week one is now a stone-cold second, a genuine arc made flesh. Geo wrenched the grand £30 League 1 (and Leagues 2 and 3) off Germany and Colombia in a single evening; Logan's Bosnia nicked League 7 off his own Cape Verde. Sean and Pete leave the night with nothing but eliminations.

Looking ahead

The bracket has kept its favourite gag warm: Logan's 🇧🇷 Brazil draw his own 🇯🇵 Japan (Mon 29 Jun) — one man certain to send himself through and knock himself out with the same whistle. Geo's 🇿🇦 South Africa face Barney's 🇨🇦 Canada (Sun 28 Jun), runner-up against runner-up, landlord against tenant once more. His 🇲🇽 Mexico meet Logan's 🇪🇨 Ecuador (Wed 1 Jul) and his 🇨🇭 Switzerland get Joe's 🇩🇿 Algeria (Fri 3 Jul). Logan's 🇲🇦 Morocco run into Joe's 🇳🇱 Netherlands (Tue 30 Jun), while his best-third 🇧🇦 Bosnia walk into Pete's Group D winners 🇺🇸 United States (Thu 2 Jul) — Old Gil, at last, with a runner in the knockouts and a grudge to nurse.

entries.title: Old Gil Banks Six, Then Draws Himself a Duel
entries.subtitle: Barney tiptoes over Geo to the summit while Ronaldo, ageless and shameless, batters Joe's Uzbeks into next week
entries.html:
There is a venerable wager beloved of seaside pier hustlers — the one where the punter is invited to bet on a coin toss, both faces of which, on closer inspection, turn out to be heads. Whatever lands, the house collects; whatever lands, the house also has to pay itself. For the entire tournament Pete has been the man on the wrong side of every coin in the building, last in the player league with the doleful patience of a fellow whose bus is always the one that breaks down. On Tuesday night, with Groups K and L sealing shut, Pete finally tossed a two-headed coin of his very own — and is now guaranteed to win and lose the exact same Round of 32 tie. Progress, of a sort.

Group K: Ronaldo declines to read the calendar

🇵🇹 Portugal 5-0 🇺🇿 Uzbekistan was Pete's seeds against Joe's stragglers, and a thoroughgoing humiliation. Cristiano Ronaldo, a man who has apparently filed retirement under "someone else's problem", volleyed in a Cancelo cross on six minutes and helped himself to a second from Bruno Fernandes on 39; Nuno Mendes curled a free-kick, Abduvohid Nematov turned one into his own net, and Rafael Leão rubber-stamped it on 87. Joe's Uzbeks finish stone-bottom on minus-nine, eleven shipped in three — the sort of leakage that would have any goalkeeper, fictional or otherwise, hurling his gloves into the stand.

Next door, 🇨🇴 Colombia 1-0 🇨🇩 Congo DR went the distance before Daniel Muñoz nodded in Quintero's pass on 76, crowning Barney's Colombians group winners on seven. Joe's Congo DR lose the match and keep the boarding pass anyway, sneaking through as a best third — a man dropping the game and pocketing the ticket.

Group L: a goalless England, a Panamanian funeral

🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 England 0-0 🇬🇭 Ghana was the night's tax return: Barney's England did just enough to top the group on seven, while Geo's Ghana clung on in third and tiptoed through as a best third with a single, blameless point — one solitary sweepstake point that, as it turned out, was nowhere near enough to keep him on the throne.

Then, in the small hours, 🇵🇦 Panama 0-1 🇭🇷 Croatia — Pete against Pete, the whole exhibit one man's property — with Ante Budimir heading the only goal on 54. Croatia march on as runners-up; Panama trudge home pointless and goalless at the bottom, beaten by their own owner and given no flowers for it.

The reckoning

This was, against all odds and a fortnight of cosmic teasing, Pete's night: six sweepstake points — his fattest single haul of the whole tournament — hauling Old Gil from ten to sixteen, though the law of the basement holds and he stays welded to sixth. The real movement was at the top, where Barney's four points lifted him from third to first on twenty-six, stepping politely over Geo, who went into the evening top and leaves it second on the same twenty-six, undone by Ghana's single timid point. Logan, idle, slips to third. And Barney's Colombia have wrenched the £30 League 3 clean off his own Canada — the rare case of a man robbing only himself and coming out richer.

Looking ahead

The bracket has handed Pete the punchline of his life. His 🇵🇹 Portugal draw his own 🇭🇷 Croatia (Fri 3 Jul) — owner against owner, the two-headed coin made flesh, Pete certain to send one of his teams into the last sixteen and bury the other with the same whistle. Elsewhere Barney owns both group winners and gets both pointed at friends: his 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 England meet Joe's third-placed 🇨🇩 Congo DR (Wed 1 Jul), the kindest of welcomes for the Three Lions, while his 🇨🇴 Colombia run into Geo's 🇬🇭 Ghana (Sat 4 Jul) — the new league leader and the man he just deposed set on a direct collision. Joe, for his sins, takes a battered Congo DR into the buzzsaw; Geo's reward for scraping third is a date with the side that just pipped him to the summit.

entries.title: Pickford Plays All Three Boards, Wins Just the One
entries.subtitle: Joe banks six and slips past Sean while Messi atones for an early miss; Sean owns both ends of France 3-0 Iraq and shrugs
entries.html:
There is an old fairground turn — the simultaneous chess exhibition — in which a single grandmaster strolls a horseshoe of tables, slapping out a move at each before the chairs have stopped creaking, so that he is at once winning brilliantly on board one, grimly holding board two, and being checkmated by a nine-year-old on board three. The crowd never quite decides whether to applaud or to fetch a doctor. On Monday night, with Groups I and J slamming shut for good, Sean walked that very horseshoe — three teams in play, one triumph, one funeral and one self-inflicted thrashing — and finished the evening graciously shaking hands with himself across an empty hall.

Group I: France stroll, Iraq sink, both in Sean's silks

🇫🇷 France 3-0 🇮🇶 Iraq was Sean versus Sean, and a thoroughly one-sided family argument: Kylian Mbappé helped himself to a brace either side of the hour, and — in a gag the fixture computer clearly wrote on purpose — Ousmane Dembélé rounded it off on 66, the surname stitched into Joe's gamertag turning up to win the game for Sean instead. France finish perfect on nine; Iraq finish stone-bottom on minus-eleven, having conceded twelve in three, the sort of leakage that would have SeandonPickford's namesake pulling his own gloves off in disgust. In the small hours 🇳🇴 Norway 3-2 🇸🇳 Senegal gave Barney the night's cleanest profit: Marcus Holmgren Pedersen and an Erling Haaland double saw off Pete's Senegalese, Ismaïla Sarr's two strikes — including one in stoppage time — merely decorating the defeat. Norway go through second; Pete's Senegal sneak the third-place ticket anyway, a man losing the game and keeping the boarding pass.

Group J: Messi's penance, Joe's tidy double

🇦🇷 Argentina 2-0 🇦🇹 Austria opened with Lionel Messi ballooning a 9th-minute penalty, then closed with Messi atoning twice — a 38th-minute opener and a 90th-minute-plus-five flourish — to send Joe's Argentines up as flawless group winners and dump Sean's Austria into second. And 🇯🇴 Jordan 1-2 🇩🇿 Algeria completed Joe's clean sweep of the evening: Nizar Al-Rashdan's first-half header had Barney's Jordanians dreaming until Nadhir Benbouali (teed up by Riyad Mahrez) and Amine Gouiri turned it round, Algeria nicking third and a qualifying spot, Jordan trudging home pointless and bottom.

The reckoning

This was Joe's night, plainly: six points from two wins haul StraitOfHorMousaDembele up to fourth and clean past Sean, who took three from France yet watched two other teams buried and dropped a place to fifth for his trouble. Barney's three keep him third on twenty-two — close enough now to smell the idle pair ahead of him, Geo (still top on twenty-five) and Logan (twenty-three), neither of whom kicked a ball. France muscled level at the summit of the grand £30 League 1, though Germany's Logan clings on up there by the finest of margins. Pete stays welded to the floor in sixth — beaten again, qualified again, Old Gil's luck running exactly true to type.

Looking ahead

The Round of 32 has stitched up a feast of grudges. Joe's perfect 🇦🇷 Argentina draw Logan's 🇨🇻 Cape Verde (Fri 3 Jul) — the buzzsaw foretold for the quiet man's draw-merchants — while his 🇩🇿 Algeria meet Geo's 🇨🇭 Switzerland (Fri 3 Jul) and his 🇮🇨🇮 Ivory Coast run into Barney's 🇳🇴 Norway (Tue 30 Jun). Joe's battered 🇸🇪 Sweden, meanwhile, get the kindest fate imaginable: Sean's 🇫🇷 France (Tue 30 Jun). And savour Sean's catch-22 — by finishing second in Group J his 🇦🇹 Austria are handed Geo's rampant, unbeaten 🇪🇸 Spain (Thu 2 Jul), owner against owner, while Algeria's third place drew the gentler Swiss; a place lower might have been a mercy. Pete's 🇸🇳 Senegal, for their pains, face Sean's 🇧🇪 Belgium (Wed 1 Jul).

entries.title: Sean Backs Both Horses in Group G
entries.subtitle: Geo strolls back to the summit as Spain spank the Saudis, while Pete watches both his runners trudge off together
entries.html:
There is a sly, bookmaker-baiting pleasure known only to the racehorse owner who saddles two runners in the same contest: whatever happens down the back straight, his colours are going to be carried home first, and he gets to look terribly gracious about the one that filled the place behind. On Sunday night, in Group G, Sean led in both the winner and the runner-up — and then, because no night is ever clean, had a third horse shot in an entirely different field.

Group G: Pickford's enclosure, twice over

🇧🇪 Belgium and 🇪🇬 Egypt are both Sean's, and both went through, top and second — the whole front of the grid in one man's silks. The catch is they got there by very different roads. Belgium ground out a goalless, joyless 0-0 with Pete's 🇮🇷 Iran, and did the last quarter-hour a man light after Nathan Ngoy walked on 66 — a clean sheet salvaged from a man-down siege, the sort of night that would have given SeandonPickford's namesake palpitations behind the sticks. Egypt did it with rather more theatre: Pete's 🇳🇿 New Zealand led through Finn Surman's 15th-minute header before Mostafa Zico, Mohamed Salah and a Trézéguet header turned it into a 3-1 stroll. Spare the loose change for Pete, who owned both losing horses in this group — Iran third and gone, New Zealand stone-bottom — and trudged off the course with a single solitary point to show for two teams.

Group H: Spain put the boot in

🇪🇸 Spain were merciless. Lamine Yamal opened on ten minutes, Mikel Oyarzabal helped himself to a three-minute brace, and a Hassan Al-Tambakti own goal after the break finished a 4-0 dismantling of Sean's 🇸🇦 Saudi Arabia — Geo's side topping the group on seven without conceding a goal all tournament, the sort of touchline-arms-folded performance ThomasTwoShell would happily take credit for. Behind them, 🇺🇾 Uruguay 2-2 🇨🇻 Cape Verde was the existential one: Logan's never-beaten Islanders drew their third in three — Kevin Pina's free-kick and Hélio Varela's 61st-minute leveller cancelling out Maxi Araújo and Agustín Canobbio's stoppage-time effort — to sneak through as runners-up without winning a match. Barney's Uruguay, two goals and all, finish third and miss the cut. The draw machine has carried Logan into the knockouts.

The reckoning

Geo went into the night second and leaves it back on the throne: three points from Spain lift him to 25 and snatch the summit clean back off Logan, who managed only the single point from Cape Verde's stalemate and slips to second on 23 — the great accumulator finally outpaced by the man he'd briefly deposed. Sean was the night's biggest mover, four points hauling him past idle Joe into fourth, even with one of his three teams battered 4-0. Logan, meanwhile, prised League 7 off Pete's New Zealand with that draw — a leader changing hands by virtue of two points scraped from three goalless-ish afternoons. Pete stays welded to the floor in sixth, an owner who put four teams into the group stage and watched the last two leave together.

Looking ahead

The bracket has cooked up a proper family-of-one feast for Sean. His 🇧🇪 Belgium draw Pete's third-placed 🇸🇳 Senegal (Wed 1 Jul) — about as kind as it gets — while his 🇪🇬 Egypt run into Geo's 🇦🇺 Australia (Fri 3 Jul). And the curio: Geo's rampant 🇪🇸 Spain meet Sean's own 🇦🇹 Austria (Thu 2 Jul), owner against owner, the leader's best side against a man already running three horses in this round. Logan's draw-merchants 🇨🇻 Cape Verde, for their pains, are handed Joe's Group J winners 🇦🇷 Argentina (Fri 3 Jul) — three honest draws rewarded with a walk straight into the buzzsaw. The quiet man's luck, it seems, only stretches so far.

entries.title: Seven Up, And It's Logan's Round
entries.subtitle: Joe bangs five past himself, ships four to Japan, and somehow still walks away with a profit
entries.html:
There survives, in the footnotes of provincial theatre, an account of a travelling troupe so threadbare that on the night the duel scene came round there was only one actor left standing — so he played both swordsmen, lunging at himself from stage left, parrying from stage right, and finally running himself through to a standing ovation, expiring in his own arms while the box office counted the takings either way. The audience adored it. The man, asked afterwards which half had won, shrugged: he had, obviously. On Saturday night, across Groups E and F, Joe revived the act in full — and StraitOfHorMousaDembele, like all great self-duellists, finished both the hero and the corpse.

Group F: Joe stabs Joe, then gets stabbed by Logan

🇳🇱 Netherlands 5-1 🇸🇪 Sweden was Joe versus Joe and a thorough massacre of one by the other: Brian Brobbey twice inside seventeen minutes, Cody Gakpo helping himself to a brace of his own after the break, and Crysencio Summerville lashing the fifth on 89 — Anthony Elanga's lone reply the only flicker from the dying man. The Dutch top the group on seven; Sweden, hammered by their own owner, still squeak through as a best third, which is the theatrical equivalent of dying onstage and being carried to the next venue regardless.

The other Joe property in Group F got no such mercy. 🇹🇳 Tunisia 0-4 🇯🇵 Japan was a clinical dismemberment by Logan's side — Daichi Kamada inside four minutes, Ayase Ueda with a brace, Junya Ito between — that sent Tunisia home stone-bottom on minus-ten and Japan through second. Joe owned three of the four teams in this group and contrived to win it, finish third in it, and prop it up.

Group E: Undav's last word, a goalless shrug

🇩🇪 Germany 2-1 🇨🇮 Ivory Coast was Logan against Joe again, and it took a while to go Logan's way: Franck Kessié nudged Joe's Ivorians ahead on the half-hour, Deniz Undav levelled on 68 and then, in the fourth minute of stoppage time, Undav struck again to snatch top spot. Cruel on Joe — except his Ivory Coast still finish runners-up, so the only thing wounded was the pride. Next door, 🇪🇨 Ecuador 0-0 🇨🇼 Curaçao was the night's tax return: Logan's Ecuador ground out the point they needed to qualify as a best third, while Barney's Curaçao bowed out with a solitary, blameless draw.

The reckoning

This was Logan's coronation. Seven points from a group winner, a runner-up and a salvaged third drag KluivertEye from third all the way to the summit — level on twenty-two with Geo but ahead of him, the idle leader watching his fortnight at the top end without lifting a boot. The man who scraped one point a day through the opening week has now banked thirteen in two nights. His 🇩🇪 Germany, meanwhile, has wrenched the grand £30 League 1 (and League 2) clean off Pete's United States. Joe's three through the Dutch nudge him up to fourth; Barney's lone point slips him to third; Sean and Pete, both idle, sit fifth and sixth, the latter watching his biggest pot change hands without a kick.

Looking ahead

The bracket has kept its private joke warm for Logan. As foretold, his 🇯🇵 Japan draw his own 🇧🇷 Brazil (Mon 29 Jun, 18:00 BST) — KluivertEye guaranteed to knock himself out of one prize and through in another, the duellist at it again. His 🇩🇪 Germany face Barney's 🇵🇾 Paraguay (Mon 29 Jun), and his 🇪🇨 Ecuador walk into Geo's 🇲🇽 Mexico (Wed 1 Jul). Joe's three survivors, by contrast, all drew daggers: his 🇳🇱 Netherlands meet Logan's 🇲🇦 Morocco (Tue 30 Jun), his 🇨🇮 Ivory Coast run into Barney's 🇳🇴 Norway (Tue 30 Jun), and his battered-but-breathing 🇸🇪 Sweden are handed Sean's 🇫🇷 France (Tue 30 Jun) — the worst possible reward for a side that already took a five-goal hiding from its own owner. The man who beat himself this week now gets beaten upon by everyone else.

entries.title: Logan's Run, At Long Last
entries.subtitle: He owns both ends of Group C, claws off the basement floor, and has somehow drawn himself in the Round of 32
entries.html:
There is a particular kind of swindler beloved of the back pages of Private Eye — the grey, unremarkable fellow nobody bothers to watch, who sits at the back of every meeting taking quiet notes while the loud men shout, and who is discovered, years later, to have owned the building, the lease and the man collecting the rent the entire time. For a fortnight Logan has been precisely that man: filed under harmless, drawing all three with Cape Verde, surviving on technicalities, drifting to fifth without a soul noticing. On Friday night KluivertEye looked up from his notebook and revealed he'd been holding both ends of the rope all along.

Group C: Logan robs the place quietly

Consider the deeds. Logan owns 🇧🇷 Brazil and 🇲🇦 Morocco — and on Friday both finished off the only two teams that weren't his. His Morocco needed barely 120 seconds against Sean's 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 Scotland, Ismael Saibari pouncing on a Brahim Díaz pass for a 2nd-minute opener that was, mercifully for Scotland, also the last word — a 1-0 that crowned Morocco runners-up and dumped Sean's Scots out third, short of the best-thirds cut and on the long road home. Then his Brazil dismantled Pete's 🇭🇹 Haiti 3-0, Matheus Cunha helping himself to a first-half brace and Vinícius Júnior rubber-stamping it on the stroke of half-time. Top and second, the whole top shelf of Group C, both Logan's. The committee minutes will record only that the trophy was awarded twice to the same man.

Group D: a win that helped nobody, a defeat that hurt nobody

Over in Group D the football turned existential. Pete's 🇺🇸 United States beat Geo's 🇦🇺 Australia 2-0 — Cameron Burgess turning into his own net on 11, Alex Freeman heading the second before the break — and yet both teams skipped through arm in arm regardless, Pete as winners, Geo as runners-up. A thumping with no casualties. The real funeral was next door: Sean's 🇹🇷 Turkey fell to a 2nd-minute Matías Galarza strike for Barney's 🇵🇾 Paraguay, then watched Miguel Almirón get himself sent off in first-half stoppage time for good measure. Paraguay sneak through as a best third; Turkey, like Scotland, are out, and Sean — top of the world only on Tuesday — banked a fat nothing while two of his teams were buried in a single night.

The reckoning

This was Logan's resurrection, plain and simple: six points from two group placings drag the great accumulator from fifth all the way to third on fifteen — the slow-burner who scored seven points in his first eight days banking six in one evening. Barney's three through Paraguay keep him serenely second, still chasing the idle Geo, who stays imperiously top on twenty-two without lifting a finger. And spare a cheer for Pete: Old Gil himself, last in the player league for what feels like forever, has finally seized something — his United States have wrestled the grand £30 League 1 (and League 2) clean off Geo's Mexico. The man who keeps losing now leads the biggest team-pot in the building. Sean and Joe, both idle, slide a place each into fourth and fifth.

Looking ahead

The bracket has saved its best gag for Logan. His 🇧🇷 Brazil draw his own 🇯🇵 Japan (Mon 29 Jun, 18:00 BST) — KluivertEye guaranteed to knock himself out of one prize while advancing in another. His 🇲🇦 Morocco face Joe's 🇳🇱 Netherlands (Tue 30 Jun), and his 🇧🇦 Bosnia must somehow stop Pete's in-form 🇺🇸 United States (Thu 2 Jul). The cruellest catch is Barney's: his 🇵🇾 Paraguay, rewarded for finishing third, draw Logan's 🇩🇪 Germany, Group E winners — a place lower might have been a mercy. Elsewhere Geo's 🇦🇺 Australia meet Sean's 🇪🇬 Egypt (Fri 3 Jul). The quiet man, it turns out, has his name on half the second round.

entries.title: Geo, Sole Proprietor of Groups A and B
entries.subtitle: Canada batter nine-man Qatar into the floorboards, and a man can lose 6-0 to himself without it costing him a penny
entries.html:
There was once, in the railway boom of the 1880s, a town in Illinois named Pullman, built and owned in its entirety by one George Pullman — every house, every shop, every church, every saloon his property, so that whatever a man earned on Monday found its way back into Pullman's pocket by Friday, the wages going out one door and the rent coming in the other. The genius of it was total: the workers could riot, strike, drink themselves stupid or vote with their feet, and George Pullman still collected. On Thursday night, across Groups A and B, the World Cup re-enacted the company town in full — and the George signing the deeds was Geo.

Group A: every farm on the estate

Consider the holdings. Geo owned all three of Group A's survivors and its eliminated third — the lot. His 🇲🇽 Mexico shut up shop against his own 🇰🇷 South Korea, Luis Romo's 50th-minute strike settling a 1-0 that crowned Mexico group winners on a perfect nine and quietly buried South Korea in third, below the best-thirds cut. A landlord raising rent on his own tenant. Earlier his 🇿🇦 South Africa needed Teboho Mokoena's 83rd-minute penalty to rescue a 1-1 against Logan's 🇨🇿 Czechia — Michal Sadílek's sixth-minute opener long since the high point of Czechia's tournament. South Africa limp through second; Czechia finish bottom and go home, Logan's solitary point his entire dividend.

Group B: the saloon takes a beating

The one parcel Geo couldn't keep tidy was 🇶🇦 Qatar, and oh, what a fire sale. Barney's 🇨🇦 Canada didn't so much win as repossess the building: Cyle Larin and Jonathan David inside half an hour, Qatar down to ten when Homam Ahmed walked on 33, then nine when Assim Madibo followed on 53, Nathan Saliba's free-kick, a Mohamed Manai own goal, and David completing his hat-trick in stoppage time for a thunderous 6-0. Two red cards, a self-inflicted seventh, and Geo's lowest seed shipped its dignity wholesale. Geo got the consolation elsewhere: his 🇨🇭 Switzerland saw off Logan's 🇧🇦 Bosnia-Herzegovina 4-1, Johan Manzambi twice and a 97th-minute Granit Xhaka penalty putting gloss on a game Bosnia had a man sent off in. Bosnia still scrape through as a best third — Logan loses the night and keeps the ticket, a trick he has now pulled so often it should carry a service charge.

The reckoning

Seven points in an evening and the empire grows: Geo went into the night top on fifteen and leaves it top on twenty-two, the cushion stretched to eight. Thomas TwoShell now leads the grand £30 League 1 and League 2 through Mexico, having shoved Germany off both perches. The night's other winner is Barney, whose six-goal landslide vaults him from fourth to second in the player league and parks Canada atop Leagues 3, 4 and 5 simultaneously — three underdog pots in one swing of David's boot. There's a delicious footnote, too: Geo's battered Qatar surrendered its lead of League 8 to Logan's never-beaten Cape Verde, a team relegated by the very hammering its own owner administered elsewhere. Sean, Joe and Pete all sat idle and watched themselves drift — Sean to third, Joe to fourth, Pete still anchored to the floor.

Looking ahead

The bracket has a sense of humour. Barney's 🇨🇦 Canada, fresh from dismantling one Geo team, draw straight into another: Geo's 🇿🇦 South Africa in the Round of 32 (Sun 28 Jun, 20:00 BST), runner-up against runner-up, owner against owner. Elsewhere Geo's 🇲🇽 Mexico land Logan's third-placed 🇪🇨 Ecuador (Wed 1 Jul) — a kindly draw for the leader — while his 🇨🇭 Switzerland meet Joe's 🇩🇿 Algeria (Fri 3 Jul). Logan's rescued 🇧🇦 Bosnia, meanwhile, must get past Pete's 🇺🇸 United States (Thu 2 Jul) — Nico Ol'Gilly's group winners against the man who keeps surviving by accident. The company town, it seems, is expanding into the knockouts.

entries.title: The Story of the Harry Kane, At Last
entries.subtitle: Barney drags himself off the canvas with both fists swinging, while Pete draws the one opponent he genuinely cannot beat — himself
entries.html:
Bob Dylan, sharpening a six-minute ballad about a man wronged, once gave the world the immortal opening line "Here comes the story of the Hurricane" — a song built entirely on the principle that the longer you are kept down, the more thunderous the rising. For a fortnight Barney has been the man kept down: rock bottom of the player league, a basement so deep it had its own postcode, his teams shipping sevens and absorbing thrashings while everyone else dined out. On Wednesday night the chorus finally dropped. Here came the story of the Harry Kane — and Harry Kane, with the comic inevitability of a gamertag coming home to roost, scored twice.

Group L: England turn it on, Croatia turn it over

🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 England 4-2 🇭🇷 Croatia was a proper old-fashioned ding-dong. Kane lashed in a 12th-minute penalty, Martin Baturina hauled Pete's Croatia level on 36, Kane nodded England back ahead before the break, and Petar Musa's 45'+5' header made it 2-2 at the interval. Then Barney's men simply had more: Jude Bellingham striking within two minutes of the restart and Marcus Rashford rubber-stamping it on 85. England top Group L on seven, perfect and purring. Croatia, beaten but unbowed, sneak through second — Pete keeps a ticket from a night he lost.

In the late kick-off, 🇬🇭 Ghana 1-0 🇵🇦 Panama was settled by the cruellest of clocks: Caleb Yirenkyi bundling home in the 90'+5' to send Geo's Ghana through third as a best third, and to dump Pete's 🇵🇦 Panama out stone-bottom, three games, three defeats, not a single goal scored. Two of Pete's teams in one group, one survived, one perished, and neither did him much good.

Group K: Colombia cruise, Joe shadow-boxes again

🇨🇴 Colombia 3-1 over 🇺🇿 Uzbekistan with the minimum of fuss — Daniel Muñoz, Luis Díaz and a Jáminton Campaz header in the ninth minute of stoppage time, Abbosbek Fayzullaev's reply a footnote — and just like that Barney had a second group winner in a single evening. Spare the loose change for Joe, whose 🇺🇿 Uzbekistan finished dead last on minus-nine, while his 🇨🇩 Congo DR ground out a 1-1 with 🇵🇹 Portugal: João Neves headed Pete's Portugal in front on six, Yoane Wissa levelled on the stroke of half-time, and the point nudged Congo DR through third. One Joe team raised from the grave, one buried in it — a familiar split for the man whose Strait remains, mercifully, wide open.

The reckoning

This was Barney's night and Barney's alone: six points from two group winners, catapulting him from rock bottom to fourth, level with Joe on eleven. The form line tells the arc — a man who scored one point in his first three days has banked nine in his last two. Geo, idle elsewhere, still pocketed three through Ghana to extend his lead at the summit to fifteen, and Ghana's late winner wrenched League 6 clean off Sean's dead-and-gone Scotland into the bargain. Joe and Pete took a thin point apiece; Pete slithers to the foot of the player league, while idle Sean holds second and Logan slides quietly to fifth without lifting a finger.

Looking ahead

The Round of 32 has cooked up a genuine curio for Pete: his 🇵🇹 Portugal meet his own 🇭🇷 Croatia on Fri 3 Jul (00:00 BST) — both teams his, so the luckless owner is guaranteed to knock himself out of one prize while advancing in another, the Old Gil special. Elsewhere Barney's bumper haul has a sting in the tail: his 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 England draw Joe's third-placed 🇨🇩 Congo DR on Wed 1 Jul (17:00 BST), and his 🇨🇴 Colombia face Geo's overachieving 🇬🇭 Ghana on Sat 4 Jul (02:30 BST) — both of Barney's group winners handed a third-placed underdog, which is about as kind as the bracket gets. Two thirds, two seeds, two chances for the resurrected man to keep his hurricane blowing.

entries.title: Sean Bookends the Group Stage, Joe Just Shadow-Boxes
entries.subtitle: France and Austria haul Pickford level at the summit while Messi spends the night thumping his own brother-in-arms — er, his own other team
entries.html:
There is an old curiosity from the early days of competitive chess, in which a club in some forgotten provincial town entered the very same member into both halves of a postal tournament under two slightly different names, purely to make the numbers up — and then watched in dawning horror as the fellow's two selves met in the final and one of them simply had to win. The committee minutes record only that the trophy was awarded, the loser declined to shake his own hand, and the whole affair was never spoken of again. Tuesday night, across two groups, the World Cup staged precisely that fixture twice — and on both occasions the man holding both name-tags was grinning.

Group I: Sean drowns and surfaces in the same evening. Sean spent the first two days of this tournament as the patron saint of nil, and now look at him — bookending an entire group. His 🇫🇷 France strolled through Senegal, Kylian Mbappé opening on 66, Bradley Barcola doubling it on 82, and after Ibrahim Mbaye's deep stoppage-time consolation for Pete's 🇸🇳 Senegal, Mbappé restored the cushion in the 96th minute for a 3-1 and top spot on a perfect nine. Pete, mercifully, sneaks through third anyway — a beaten man who keeps his ticket. Then the dark comedy: Sean's other Group I side, 🇮🇶 Iraq, were dismantled 1-4 by Barney's 🇳🇴 Norway, Erling Haaland helping himself to a first-half brace and poor Aymen Hussein contriving to both score Iraq's lone header and bundle into his own net at 90'+6'. One Sean team finished first, the other dead last and minus-eleven — the man owns the penthouse and the pavement.

Group J: Joe versus Joe, refereed by Messi. Over in Group J, Joe staged the night's purest exhibition of futility-by-success: his 🇦🇷 Argentina against his 🇩🇿 Algeria, a contest he could neither lose nor enjoy. Lionel Messi didn't care for the subtlety and simply helped himself to a hat-trick — 17, 60, 76 — a 3-0 that sent Argentina top and Algeria limping out as a third-placed qualifier. Both Joe's; three points the entire haul. Meanwhile Sean's 🇦🇹 Austria edged Barney's 🇯🇴 Jordan 3-1, Ali Olwan's equaliser cancelled by Yazan Al-Arab's own goal and finished off by Marko Arnautovic's penalty deep into a frankly absurd twelfth minute of stoppage time. Austria second, Jordan bottom and gone.

The reckoning. Six points in a single night drags Sean from fourth all the way to joint-top on twelve — level with the idle Geo, who could only watch his cushion evaporate without a ball being kicked. From three days of nothing to the summit: SeanDonPickford has caught his breath at last, and his Austria has wrestled League 4 clean off Geo's Australia into the bargain. Joe's three nudge him to ten and third. Barney's brace of results — a thrashing dished out, a defeat absorbed — earns three honest points but leaves him propping up the player table. Logan, untroubled tonight, slides quietly from second to fourth. Pete banks nothing but, Gil-like, escapes the group anyway.

Looking ahead. The Round of 32 is a minefield laced with familiar faces. Sean's France draw Joe's 🇸🇪 Sweden on Tue 30 Jun — the in-form man against Joe's lucky leftovers — while Sean's Austria, having earned runners-up status, are rewarded with the cruellest cushion of all: Geo's 🇪🇸 Spain on Thu 2 Jul, surely the night Austria wished it had finished a place lower. Pete's battered Senegal must somehow rouse themselves against Sean's 🇧🇪 Belgium on Wed 1 Jul, and Barney's Norway run into Joe's 🇨🇮 Ivory Coast on Tue 30 Jun. Joe, meanwhile, faces a split personality: his Argentina meet Logan's peaceable 🇨🇻 Cape Verde on Fri 3 Jul, and that same dawn his 🇩🇿 Algeria collide with Geo's 🇨🇭 Switzerland — the one tie where the brothers finally point their pistols squarely at each other.

entries.title: The Monday Football Forgot How to Win
entries.subtitle: Four matches, four draws, two men solemnly shaking hands with themselves — and Sean accidentally assembling an empire out of pure stalemate
entries.html:
Somewhere in the dusty annals of the Spanish board game there is the legend of the eternal chess match between two grandmasters so evenly matched, so terrified of error, that they shoved their pieces about for nine hours and agreed a draw before either had lost a pawn — and then ordered the same lunch. Monday night was that match stretched across four stadiums. Not one game produced a winner. Eight teams took the field; eight teams left with the smug, bloodless expression of men who'd decided the safest thing to do with a coin was to balance it on its edge. The World Cup, briefly, turned pacifist.

Group H: the diplomats of nil

🇪🇸 Spain and 🇨🇻 Cape Verde Islands played out a 0-0 that suited everyone and thrilled no one. Geo's Spain were never going to be caught — top of the group on seven, five scored, none conceded, the Thomas TwoShell tactics board humming along in serene, scoreless autopilot. But the night's quiet marvel belongs to Logan: his Cape Verde have qualified for the knockout stage of a World Cup having drawn all three games — three honourable handshakes, two goals, nought lost, second place secured by the diplomatic arts alone. A point apiece sent both through, which is the only outcome that could leave Geo and Logan equally unbothered.

Meanwhile 🇸🇦 Saudi Arabia and 🇺🇾 Uruguay staged the saddest 1-1 of the lot. Abdulelah Al-Amri put Sean's Saudis ahead on 41, only for Maxi Araújo to level for Barney's Uruguay on 80 — and it mattered not a jot, because both were already doomed, Saudi bottom and Uruguay third and a fraction short of the best-thirds cut. Barney's StoryOfTheHarryKane heavyweights came to the carnival and went home minus-one, a single dead point their entire reward.

Group G: Sean drew with Sean, and won twice

The week's strangest profit centre. 🇧🇪 Belgium versus 🇪🇬 Egypt was a contest only Sean could lose and only Sean could win — both were his. Emam Ashour, fed inevitably by Mohamed Salah, gave Egypt the lead on 20, and Belgium were rescued not by their own boots but by poor Mohamed Hany turning into his own net on 66. SeanDonPickford, the man who'd spent the group stage flapping at everything, somehow has both his Group G sides marching into the Round of 32, top and second, banked for the price of a single self-administered handshake.

And then 🇮🇷 Iran 2-2 🇳🇿 New Zealand — another civil war, another owner playing both ends, except this time the house lost. Elijah Just helped himself to a brace, Chris Wood assisting both, with Ramin Rezaeian and Mohammad Mohebbi hauling Pete's Iran level each time. Four goals, much honest endeavour, and both teams eliminated regardless: Iran third and short, New Zealand bottom. Vintage Old Gil — the lift doors opening on an empty shaft.

The reckoning

Geo nudged to twelve and stays imperiously top, though a single point hardly extends a lead. Logan's Cape Verde draw keeps him second on eight. Sean is the night's sly mover: three points from three stalemates lift him above Pete into fourth, his tournament resurrected from the morgue. Pete banked two but loses both teams and slips to fifth — small mercy that his eliminated New Zealand has, by the daft arithmetic of the underdog tiers, snatched the lead of the £30 League 7 off Logan's Bosnia. A dead team, leading a live league. Barney stays rooted to the floor.

Looking ahead

The draw has been kind and cruel in equal measure. Sean's revival faces an immediate civil tax: his 🇪🇸-conquering 🇧🇪 Belgium draw 🇸🇳 Senegal (Pete's) on Wed 1 Jul, while his 🇪🇬 Egypt run into Geo's 🇦🇺 Australia on Fri 3 Jul — and most delicious of all, Geo's 🇪🇸 Spain meet 🇦🇹 Austria, which is also Sean's, on Thu 2 Jul, so Sean is guaranteed a survivor and a casualty in one tie. Spare the candle for Logan: his peaceable, never-beaten Cape Verde have earned, for all their diplomacy, 🇦🇷 Argentina — Joe's Group J winners — on Fri 3 Jul. The pacifists, at last, meet the firing squad.

entries.title: Joe Strolls In and Robs the Room Blind
entries.subtitle: Three days fashionably absent, one night and seven points later — while Logan books himself for fratricide and Barney ships seven
entries.html:
There is a particular species of dinner guest — every table has known one — who ignores the invitation's stated hour entirely, lets the others fret over the canapés and the small talk and the awkward business of the seating plan, and then sweeps in somewhere around the main course, full of charm, untroubled, and proceeds to eat more than anyone while complaining the wine has been opened too long. For three days Joe was that empty chair: a man with a fistful of teams and not a single point to show for them, his name absent from the player league altogether. On Sunday night he sat down, unfurled his napkin, and devoured the lot.

Group F: a feast laid entirely for one

The 🇸🇪 Sweden versus 🇹🇳 Tunisia fixture was, on paper, a contest. In Joe's ledger it was a man playing chess against his own reflection and shaking his own hand afterwards. Yasin Ayari opened on seven and shut the door in the 90'+6', Alexander Isak helping himself to a goal and three assists in a 5-1 demolition that sent Joe's Sweden through as a best third and dumped Joe's Tunisia out bottom on nil — every goal, both ways, billed to the same account. Earlier his 🇳🇱 Netherlands led twice through Van Dijk and Summerville, only for Logan's 🇯🇵 Japan to answer twice, Daichi Kamada's 89th-minute header nicking a 2-2 that left the Dutch top of the group regardless and Japan safely second. A point for Logan, three for the Oranje — Joe couldn't lose if he tried, and he barely did.

Group E: Diallo at the death

Joe's 🇨🇮 Ivory Coast had left it agonisingly late before — and did again, Amad Diallo's 90th-minute strike, teed up by Singo, breaking Logan's 🇪🇨 Ecuador 1-0 and snatching the runners-up berth. Ecuador limped through third anyway, so Logan keeps the team while losing the night. The slaughter, meanwhile, belonged to Logan's 🇩🇪 Germany, who put seven past Barney's 🇨🇼 Curaçao — a Havertz double, Undav, Musiala, Schlotterbeck, Nmecha, the works — Livano Comenencia's 21st-minute reply the loneliest goal of the weekend. Barney's plucky minnows go home minus-eight; Barney himself stays nailed to the foot of the player league.

The reckoning

Joe is the night's bandit-in-chief: seven points from a standing start, vaulting from non-existent to third in the player league in a single sitting. Logan banked four — a German rout and a Japanese point — to climb above an idle Pete into second, and crucially his Germany has seized League 1 and League 2 from Pete's USA, the two grand £30 prizes both swinging KluivertEye's way. Joe's Sweden snatched the lead of League 3 off Geo's Australia for good measure. Geo, idle, stays top of the player race on eleven — but the chasers are now breathing on his collar. Pete slips to fourth without kicking a ball, Sean and Barney becalmed.

Looking ahead

The Round of 32 has arranged a genuine horror for Logan: his 🇯🇵 Japan draws his own 🇧🇷 Brazil on Mon 29 Jun (18:00 BST) — the only head-to-head where the two combatants share a single owner, and the rare night the Joe–Geo dynamic stays out of it entirely. Joe's 🇳🇱 Netherlands meets Logan's 🇲🇦 Morocco on Tue 30 Jun, while his 🇨🇮 Ivory Coast lands a kindly-looking 🇳🇴 Norway (Barney's). Spare the sympathy, though, for his 🇸🇪 Sweden: third place earned them Sean's 🇫🇷 France, Group I winners — Sean's lone survivor walking into Joe's overachieving leftovers on Tue 30 Jun (22:00 BST). And on Wed 1 Jul, Logan's 🇪🇨 Ecuador must somehow get past Geo's 🇲🇽 Mexico. The buffet, it seems, is only just being laid out.

entries.title: The Duellist Who Hired Both Pistols
entries.subtitle: Geo and Logan each watch two of their own teams cancel out, while Sean scores at his own funeral
entries.html:
There is a grim little anecdote from the duelling days of old Europe about a nobleman so determined to settle a point of honour that, finding no second man willing to face him, he simply funded both ends of the affair: his own pistol and his opponent's, his own surgeon and the other fellow's priest, the carriage there and the coffin back. Whoever fell at dawn, he had paid for the bullet — a man who could not lose the duel because he had already lost the chequebook. On Saturday night the World Cup served up two such honour-killings, and at each dawn the bill landed on a single doormat.

Group B: Geo versus Geo, again

🇶🇦 Qatar and 🇨🇭 Switzerland, both Geo's, met in a fixture only he could care about, and only he could grumble at. Breel Embolo's 17th-minute penalty had the Swiss serenely on course — until, with the clock reading 90'+4', poor Miro Muheim turned the ball into his own net to gift Qatar a 1-1 and their solitary, dignity-preserving point. Switzerland still strolls out as group winners on seven; Qatar finishes rock bottom, minus-eight, eliminated, but cruelly hands Geo the lead of the underdog League 8 on the way down. A draw with himself: one point banked, one own goal mourned, the Thomas TwoShell ledger both up and down at once.

Group C: Logan's house divided

Then the encore. 🇧🇷 Brazil and 🇲🇦 Morocco — both Logan's — staged their own pistols-at-dawn in Group C. Ismael Saibari, fed by Brahim Díaz, put Morocco ahead on 21; Vinícius Júnior, teed up by Bruno Guimarães, levelled on 32; and there it stayed, 1-1, sending both of KluivertEye's sides through, Brazil top on seven, Morocco second on seven. Two qualifiers, two sweepstake points, and not a single soul to gloat at across the bar.

The corpse that scored

The night's most poignant footnote belonged to Sean, a man who arrived on three nil and desperate. His 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 Scotland actually won — John McGinn's 28th-minute strike sinking Pete's hapless 🇭🇹 Haiti 1-0, a third straight defeat that leaves Old Gil's islanders bottom, pointless and gone. Three sweepstake points for Seandon Pickford, his first of the tournament, and yet Scotland still finishes third, misses the best-thirds cut and packs its bags regardless: a goal at its own graveside. Worse still for Sean, his 🇹🇷 Turkey were simultaneously dismantled 2-0 by Geo's 🇦🇺 Australia — Nestory Irankunda on 27, Connor Metcalfe on 75 — and dumped out fourth. Australia, meanwhile, sail through as runners-up.

The reckoning

Geo is, predictably, the night's accountant-in-chief: five points from a Swiss draw, a Qatari draw and an Aussie win, up to eleven and still imperious atop the player league. His Australia has seized the lead of Leagues 3, 4 and 5, and Qatar nicked League 8 — four tables tilting his way in a single evening. Logan adds two and climbs quietly. The black comedy, though, is at the foot: Sean's three points vault him above an idle Barney into fourth, and his dead Scotland now leads the underdog League 6 — a £30 prize being contested by a team already on the plane home. Pete and Barney blanked.

Looking ahead, the Round of 32 has laid its mines. Geo's Switzerland draws 🇩🇿 Algeria — and Algeria belongs to Joe, so the two brothers are flung head-to-head for real on Fri 3 Jul (04:00 BST). The same morning, Geo's Australia faces 🇪🇬 Egypt, which is — improbably — still-breathing Sean, his lone survivor after Turkey and Scotland perished. And spare a thought for Logan, condemned to a sequel of his own civil war: his Brazil meets his own 🇯🇵 Japan on Mon 29 Jun (18:00 BST), a tie he cannot lose and cannot truly win, while his Morocco walks straight into Joe's 🇳🇱 Netherlands on Tue 30 Jun — the duellist, once more, paying for every pistol on the field.

entries.title: Old Gil Finally Catches a Break
entries.subtitle: Balogun's brace plants Pete's flag on the summit while Sean's Turkey slinks home unnoticed
entries.html:
There is a recurring fellow in the great American cartoon — perennially out of luck, forever fumbling the briefcase, the man for whom the lift doors always close one second too soon. Pete has spent two days wearing that very expression under the Nico Ol'Gilly banner, watching Geo hog the headlines. And then, on a humid night in Group D, the lift doors held open. Old Gil walked in. He even got a seat.

USA 4-1 Paraguay — Pete buries Barney

🇺🇸 United States did not so much win as conduct an orchestra of Paraguayan misery. Damián Bobadilla turned into his own net on seven minutes, Folarin Balogun helped himself to a brace either side of the break — the second deep in first-half stoppage time, set up by Tillman — and even a 52nd-minute red card for Tim Ream couldn't stop the rout, Giovanni Reyna nodding the fourth in the 98th minute as 🇵🇾 Paraguay were still recounting the disaster. Maurício's 73rd-minute consolation was precisely that. For Pete this is rocket fuel: USA finish top of Group D and, more thrillingly, his stars and stripes have dethroned Geo's Mexico at the head of League 1 and League 2 — the grand prizes now leaning Pete's way for the first time. Three points banked, second in the player league, and the briefcase, for once, unfumbled.

Spare a thought for Barney, who owned the losing side and could only sit and absorb it. And spare a colder thought for Sean, whose 🇹🇷 Turkey didn't even need to take the field to be confirmed dead — pipped to a qualifying spot by the very Paraguay that just got hammered, finishing fourth and bottom of the section, and dragging Sean's tournament out with them. SeanDonPickford has yet to trouble the scoreboard at all. Distribution remains a problem.

Canada 1-1 Bosnia — Barney and Logan share the spoils

Earlier, 🇨🇦 Canada and 🇧🇦 Bosnia-Herzegovina staged the most civilised of stitch-ups, both knowing a point would likely do the trick. Jovo Lukic's 21st-minute header, teed up by Kolasinac, had Logan's Bosnians ahead until Cyle Larin scrambled level on 78 from Promise David's cross. The handshake was a formality: Canada qualify as Group B runners-up behind Geo's serene 🇨🇭 Switzerland (seven points, untroubled), and Bosnia squeak through as a best third. A point each, a friend each — Barney and Logan walking away arm in arm, both off the mark. Geo's other Group B holding, 🇶🇦 Qatar, finished bottom on a single point and minus-eight, the one blot on an otherwise immaculate ledger.

The reckoning

Pete is the night's undisputed winner: three points, the player league's runner-up berth out of nowhere, and his name now atop the two leagues that matter most. Geo, idle tonight, watched his throne in Leagues 1 and 2 quietly removed beneath him while still leading the player race on six. Logan, of all people, becomes a league leader — Bosnia now tops Leagues 5, 6 and 7, the underdog tiers crowning KluivertEye almost by accident. Barney scrapes a point and fourth. Sean scrapes nothing and goes home.

Looking ahead

The Round of 32 has been gleefully cruel to Barney. His battered Paraguay, third-placed and lucky to be here, have drawn 🇩🇪 Germany — Logan's Germany, Group E winners — on Mon 29 Jun (21:30 BST): a buzzsaw of the highest order. Meanwhile his Canada, having finished the dizzy heights of runner-up, land the gentler 🇿🇦 South Africa (Geo's) on Sun 28 Jun — proof that climbing higher sometimes just earns you a softer cushion. And savour Thu 2 Jul (01:00 BST): Logan's Bosnia versus Pete's all-conquering USA, KluivertEye's underdogs walking straight into Old Gil's good week.

entries.title: Geo Runs the Table — Literally
entries.subtitle: A man who owns three-quarters of a group cannot lose, except in the one place it counts
entries.html:
There is an old wheeze among riverboat gamblers that the surest way to win a hand of poker is to deal yourself everybody else's cards too, and on the opening night of this whole circus Geo arrived at the table having quietly bought three of the four chairs in Group A. Mexico his, South Africa his, South Korea his — a one-man cartel in green, gold and red, leaving poor Logan clutching Czechia like the last guest at a party he didn't realise was a stitch-up.

Mexico 2-0 South Africa — Geo versus Geo

Quite how a man is supposed to celebrate this is a theological question for the ages. 🇲🇽 Mexico took Julián Quiñones' ninth-minute opener and never looked back, Raúl Jiménez nodding in a 67th-minute header to seal it, while 🇿🇦 South Africa — also Geo's, lest anyone forget — committed footballing hara-kiri with two red cards, Sithole off after the break and Zwane following on 84 minutes, finishing the night with nine men and a thousand-yard stare. Mexico even got a red of their own through César Montes deep in stoppage time, as if to insist on fairness. The upshot: Mexico march out as group winners on a flawless nine points and a goal difference of plus-six, South Africa limp through as runners-up anyway. Both Geo's. The Thomas TwoShell tactics board was, for once, never going to be wrong.

South Korea 2-1 Czechia — the cruellest kind of win

And here is where the gods got their pound of flesh. 🇰🇷 South Korea, yet another Geo holding, fell behind to a Ladislav Krejčí header on 59 minutes and looked dead — until Hwang In-Beom levelled and then turned provider for Oh Hyeon-Gyu's 80th-minute winner. A glorious comeback. A famous victory. And utterly, magnificently pointless, because Korea finish third and miss the best-thirds cut, eliminated despite winning their final game. Three sweepstake points in Geo's back pocket, a tournament exit in the same trouser. 🇨🇿 Czechia, meanwhile, prop up the table on a single point, dumped out bottom, and KluivertEye's grand conspiracy theory tonight is simply that the fixture computer hates him personally.

The reckoning

Only two men had skin in tonight's game and the scoreboard is brutal in its simplicity: Geo banked six points — a Mexico three, a Korea three — and goes straight to the summit of the player league, top of the pile he has barely had time to read. Logan sits second on nil, which sounds gentler than it is when second of two is also last of two. Geo's stranglehold extends across the team-leagues too: Mexico leads League 1 and League 2, South Korea heads Leagues 3 and 4, while Logan's Czechia, by the strange mathematics of the underdog tiers, inherits the lead in Leagues 5 and 6 purely for being lowly enough to qualify for them — a leadership of zero points that may not survive the week. Geo even tops League 7 with South Africa. One man, half the trophies on the mantelpiece, and a freshly eliminated team he owns to mourn. Curious life.

Looking ahead

The Round of 32 has served up a delicious double helping. Mexico's reward for topping the group is a date with 🇪🇨 Ecuador on Wed 1 Jul (02:00 BST) — and Ecuador belongs to none other than Logan, scrambling through as a Group E third. So Geo and Logan, the only two combatants of opening night, are flung straight back into the ring, this time with Geo's flag-bearers favourites against Logan's battered survivor. Revenge, served chilled, on a school night. South Africa, the nine-man runners-up, draw 🇨🇦 Canada — that's Barney's Canada — on Sun 28 Jun (20:00 BST), a tie Geo will quietly fancy and Barney will quietly dread. For Korea and Czechia, there is only the long flight home and the cold comfort of a job, in one case, very nearly done.
